findings.claim: syncLayersOnce marks a layer clean (`dirty = false`) before its upload starts, and writes the new `ref` only after the await. A copy of the layer taken during that window, by duplicateLayer or by a `layers` undo record (snapshotLayer), gets `dirty: false` together with the OLD ref and the NEW pixels. Nothing uploads that copy again, so its file is the version from before the stroke.
findings.scenario: A 15k layer L already has a stored file. The user paints on it, waits for the 15 s autosave (scheduleAutosave -> syncLayers), and while its PNG uploads (1-3 s at 15k) presses Ctrl+J. duplicateLayer sets copy.ref = L.ref (old), because L.dirty is false at that moment, and copy.dirty = false || !oldRef = false; copy.px is a clone of the painted pixels. The upload then gives only L its new ref. The copy is never stored again: getValue, the autosave and a .scumble save (flushEditor -> syncLayers skips it) all name the old file, so after a restart or a reopen the copy shows the picture from before the stroke. The same happens with a reorder, delete, group or merge (a `layers` step) during the upload followed by Ctrl+Z: the restored record holds the painted px with the old ref and dirty false. recheckRestoredFiles does not catch it either, because the old file still exists.
findings.evidence: inpaint_canvas.js 889-913: `layer.dirty = false;` at 892, then `await uploadPixels(...)`, then `layer.ref = ref` (the mask: 900-904 the same). inpaint_ed_layers.js duplicateLayer 307: `ref: layer.dirty ? null : layer.ref, dirty: !!layer.dirty || !layer.ref`, and copy.px = layer.px.clone() at 315. inpaint_ed_history.js snapshotLayer 174-175 (`{ ...l }` keeps ref and dirty). applySnapshot `layers` 571-583 brings the records back as they are and uploads nothing (its comment says so). recheckRestoredFiles 859-866 asks only whether the old file is gone. The trigger is inpaint_ed_filters.js 287-293 (the autosave 15 s after the last change).
findings.fix: Treat a layer whose upload is in flight as dirty to anyone who copies it. One way: syncLayersOnce sets `layer._uploading = layer.px` before the await and clears it after. duplicateLayer and snapshotLayer then use `dirty: true, ref: null` (and the same for maskDirty / maskRef) while `_uploading` is set. Another way: keep `dirty` true during the upload and clear it afterwards only if a per-layer change counter (bumped by markLayerChanged / markMaskChanged) has not moved.
findings.why:
The claim holds. I read the code at ce4415ec.

**The window exists.** `inpaint_canvas.js` 890-913 (`syncLayersOnce`) sets `layer.dirty = false` before `await uploadPixels(layer.px, ...)` and writes `layer.ref = ref` only after the await. `maskDirty` / `maskRef` work the same way (900-909). For a 15k layer the PNG encode plus the upload takes seconds, so the window is real at the size the app is tuned for.

**A copy taken in that window keeps the old file.** `duplicateLayer` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js` 301-325) has no busy or sync guard. It sets `ref: layer.dirty ? null : layer.ref` (the old ref, because `dirty` is already false), `dirty: !!layer.dirty || !layer.ref` (false), and `copy.px = layer.px.clone()` (the painted pixels). When the upload finishes, only the original object gets the new ref.

**An undo step taken in that window does the same.** `snapshotLayer` (`inpaint_ed_history.js` ~172) is `{ ...l }`, so a `layers` step records the old ref with `dirty: false` and the shared, painted px. `applySnapshot` `layers` (~571-583) brings those records back as they are. `recheckRestoredFiles` (~858-870) only re-uploads a layer whose file has gone from the store, and the old file is still there.

**Nothing later catches it.** `flushEditor` (`host_documents.js` 29-45) only syncs layers with `dirty && px`, so the copy or restored layer is skipped. A .scumble save, the autosave and getValue then name the pre-stroke file, and after a reopen or restart the layer shows the picture from before the stroke.

**How a user hits it.** In the undo case the user's original layer itself loses the stroke on reload, not just a copy. The trigger is the autosave 15 s after the last change, so the user's next action after a pause, such as Ctrl+J or a reorder, delete or group followed by Ctrl+Z, can land inside the upload. That makes it a narrow but realistic way to lose pixels.

**Not a repeat.** I found nothing on `syncLayersOnce` / `duplicateLayer` / `snapshotLayer` for this in `docs/BUGS.md` or either `verified.json`. The full review's `syncLayersOnce` mention is about the MCP quit kill, which is a different defect.

**The fix direction is right.** Copies taken during an upload should count as dirty: either an in-flight marker, or keep `dirty` true until the upload is done and clear it only if a per-layer change counter has not moved since.

findings.claim: A filter layer's limit has two rules, and only the Canvas 2D path applies them. In filteredCanvas a non-plain layer (blend mode, opacity, mask, clip) gets `info.limitOver = true`, so the limit's weight goes into the result's alpha, and a missing depth map makes the layer draw nothing (canvas = null). filterInfo, which is shared with the tiles program's bandFilter, sets neither. In the tiles program the limit stage therefore uses mix(in, out, w), and a missing map hands the input back. programFinish then composites that band over itself in the layer's blend mode.
findings.scenario: Tiles backend (the default). A Black & white or Curves filter layer in Multiply, Screen, Overlay or Soft light, with a luma limit (say 0.6..1, highlights only). On screen the layer shows nothing outside the range. A plain PNG export (bandSource -> programBand), a run's crop (readBoxBytes, how 'program', the picture a paid API run is sent) and frequency separation instead get I multiply I (or screen, overlay ...) there: the shadows come out darkened or lightened. A depth limit whose map is missing (`limitMissing`) does the same over the whole layer, fill layers included. The same document exports correctly with a Size row (the canvas path), so screen, sized export and plain export disagree.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_filters.js:623-627 sets `info.limitOver = !plain` only in filteredCanvas. :635-636 turns a limitMissing pass-through into null (draw nothing) only there. filterInfo :518-553 sets neither. inpaint_ed_stack.js:351-368 bandFilter calls filterInfo and applyFilter, then returns `out || input`. inpaint_limit.js:70 `over = def.over || info.limitOver`, so `mix(i, c, w)` (LIMIT_SHADER :41, CPU :184-187) is used. inpaint_limit.js:61-63 returns `src` with limitMissing. stackPlan :167-181 admits filter layers with a blend (OPS has multiply..luminosity), opacity, mask or limit. holdStackNow :259 marks them non-plain. programFinish :461-469 reads `out` and composites it over the band with `st.op` / `st.alpha` / `st.mask`, so where w = 0 the band is blended with itself.
findings.fix: Make the rule part of the shared pass info. Have filterInfo take `plain` (or bandFilter pass the step's `st.plain`) and set `info.limitOver = !plain` for every caller. In bandFilter, when `info.limitMissing` and the result is the input for a non-plain step, return a transparent result (or tell programFinish to skip the composite), as filteredCanvas returns null. Add a limit_test / composite_test case: a luma-limited levels layer in multiply, comparing the screen, flattenToCanvas and programBand bytes.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. In inpaint_ed_filters.js, `filteredCanvas` (line 627) sets `info.limitOver = !plain`. At line 636 it turns a `limitMissing` pass-through into null, so the layer draws nothing. `filterInfo` (518-553) sets neither, and `limitOver` is not set anywhere else in renderer/: the only other mention is a comment in inpaint_limit.js. `_filterInfoHook` is a test hook.

`bandFilter` (inpaint_ed_stack.js 351-368) calls `filterInfo` and then `applyFilter`. `applyFilter` runs `limitStage` (inpaint_filters.js:1448), and `bandFilter` returns `out || input`. In `limitStage`, `over = def.over || info.limitOver` (inpaint_limit.js:70), so a non-fill filter takes `mix(i, c, w)` in the shader (:41) and in the CPU path (:184-187). A depth limit with no map returns `src` (:61-63).

`stackPlan` (stack.js 167-181) lets a filter layer through with a blend (OPS), an opacity or a mask, and never checks for a limit. `holdStackNow` marks such a step non-plain (:259). The program loop (~461-469) then reads the filter's output and composites it with `st.op` / `st.alpha` / `st.mask` over the band it was made from. Where w = 0 that output is the input itself, so the band gets multiplied, screened or overlaid with itself. With a missing depth map the whole layer does that.

This path really runs. Exports go through it (composite.js:683 `holdStack(stackPlan({filters: true}))` -> `programReader`), and so do `readBoxBytes` and the run's crop (stack.js 738/754). On the default tiles backend it is taken whenever the plan qualifies.

The existing test does not catch it. limit_test.py case 0 (multiply levels with a luma limit) checks only `flattenToCanvas`, which is the canvas `filteredCanvas` path. The fix of 91fe5094 ("the limit's weight in the alpha under a blend mode") went into that path only.

The finding is not in BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for limitOver / bandFilter / limit under a blend mode). The suggested fix direction is right: set `limitOver` from the step's `plain` in `bandFilter` (or in `filterInfo`), and in `bandFilter` return a transparent or skipped result for a non-plain `limitMissing`.

Severity must: on tiles, a plain export and the crop sent to a paid run silently differ from the screen, with shadows darkened or lightened wherever the limit is 0.

findings.claim: ask() sets `this.askOpen = wrap` without closing a question that is already open. The first question's backdrop stays in the DOM (inset 0, z-index 20) over the whole editor. Its finish() returns early because `this.askOpen !== wrap`, so its buttons, Escape and Enter do nothing and its promise never resolves.
findings.scenario: The editor's New dialog, Snapshot, Clear undo history or Clean up files question is open (or Image > Frequency Separation... is). The user then picks Image > Frequency Separation... or Image > Split into Layers... from the app's native menu bar, which stays reachable while the editor's overlay is up. menuCommand calls frequencySeparation() or openSplitDialog() with no askOpen check, and they call ed.ask again. After the second question is answered, the first backdrop stays on top of the editor and cannot be dismissed. The editor cannot be used until the tab is closed, and the first caller (for example newCanvas) waits forever.
findings.evidence: inpaint_canvas.js ask: finish at 631-639 starts with `if (this.askOpen !== wrap) return;` (632); 653 `this.askOpen = wrap;` and 655 `this._askFinish = finish;` overwrite the earlier question's without finishing it. closeAsk (inpaint_ed_view.js 578-582) finishes only the current _askFinish. shell.js menuCommand 1272 frequency-separation -> frequencySeparation (1206-1210, calls ed.ask with no askOpen guard) and 1276 split-layers -> splitdialog.js openSplitDialog (26-48, editor.ask with no guard). The shell's key handlers at 1119 and 1251 do check askOpen, so the code assumes one question at a time. Style: inpaint_style.js 51 `.ipc-ask { position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:20 }`.
findings.fix: At the top of ask(), if `this._askFinish` is set, call `this.closeAsk()` so the earlier question answers null and removes its backdrop. Or refuse the new one (resolve null at once) while `this.askOpen` is set, and guard frequencySeparation and openSplitDialog on askOpen as the shell's key handlers do.
findings.why:
I read the code and it holds. In inpaint_canvas.js, ask() at 653/655 sets this.askOpen = wrap and this._askFinish = finish with no check for a question already open. The earlier question's finish (631-639) begins with `if (this.askOpen !== wrap) return;`, so after the second question replaces it, its Cancel, OK and backdrop click do nothing. Once the second question is answered, askOpen is null, so the first one's finish still returns early. closeAsk (inpaint_ed_view.js 578-582) only reaches the current _askFinish, which the second finish has already cleared. The path really runs. main.js 773 and 780 send "frequency-separation" and "split-layers" from the native Image menu, which stays reachable because the question is a div inside the editor root, not a modal. menuCommand (shell.js 1272, 1276) calls frequencySeparation() (1206-1214) and openSplitDialog() (splitdialog.js 26-48), and both call ed.ask without checking askOpen. The shell's key handlers (1119, 1251) do check askOpen, which shows the code assumes one question at a time.

It is worse than the reviewer says. The first question's window capture listener onKey (640-649) stays registered, and its wrap stays connected. So on every Escape or Enter it calls preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation, then a finish that does nothing. Because it was registered first, it takes Enter and Escape even from the second question, and after that from every field in the window, until the tab is destroyed. Meanwhile the first caller's promise (newCanvas, snapshot and so on) never resolves.

This is not known. The review_full_2026-11-07 finding at verified.json:373 is about a question in a background tab answering keys typed in another tab, and close() leaking the listener; those are what the isConnected/_destroyed checks and _askFinish address. This finding is a second ask on the same editor, and nothing in BUGS.md covers it.

Severity is should: a stuck state that blocks the editor and swallows keys, with no pixel loss, reached through a plausible but uncommon menu pick. The suggested fix is right: call closeAsk() at the top of ask() when _askFinish is set, or refuse the new question while askOpen is set. Either way the menu entries should also check askOpen, as the key handlers do.

findings.claim: setValue checks only its own `_loadToken` after each await, and loadFile checks only `_openToken`. A picture opened into a tab while that tab's document is still loading gets a new base (setBasePixels clears the layers), and then the restore goes on: it pushes the old document's remaining layers, selection, maps, history, saved selections and guides onto the new picture.
findings.scenario: A 15k document with several layers is restored at start, reopened or opened into a tab. setValue has set the base and is decoding the layers one after another (seconds each). The user clicks the editor's Open button or Ctrl+drops a file on the canvas. loadFile -> setBasePixels(keepLayers: false) empties the layers and the undo. setValue's loop then pushes the rest of the old layers (old positions and sizes), draws the old selection into the new one, and sets maps (a depth map of the other picture), history and guides. The autosave then stores that mix as the tab's document. Crop, turn and resize already refuse during a load (turnBlocked checks _loading), but loadFile, the node's newCanvas and the drop handlers do not.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_persist.js setValue 105 `const stale = () => this._loadToken !== token;`. After each layer's await (190-240) only stale() is checked, then `this.layers.push(...)` (196, 233). Then selection 270-288, maps 312-332, history 258-262. inpaint_ed_open.js loadFile 139-145: its own `_openToken`, no look at `_loading` and no bump of `_loadToken`. setBasePixels 98-126 resets the layers and the undo but not `_loadToken`. Entry points with no guard: inpaint_modal.js 92-96 (Open button), inpaint_canvas.js 453 (Ctrl+drop), inpaint_ed_chrome.js 40 (the node widget's drop). inpaint_ed_geometry.js 628 shows the intended rule (`this._loading` blocks geometry changes).
findings.fix: Have setBasePixels (or loadFile) bump `this._loadToken` when it does not run from inside setValue itself, so a restore in flight stops at its next stale() check. Or refuse loadFile and newCanvas while `this._loading` is set ('the document is still loading'), as host_pictures.js 401 and turnBlocked already do.
findings.why:
I read the code at ce4415ec and the claim holds. setValue (inpaint_ed_persist.js 104-106) sets its own `_loadToken`, sets `_loading`, and after every await checks only `stale()`, which compares `_loadToken` (lines 121, 125, 181-191, 221-231, 265-267, 287-291, 334). It then pushes the old layers (`this.layers.push`, persist 169 / 196 / 233) and sets the selection, maps and history. loadFile (inpaint_ed_open.js 139-145) has its own `_openToken` / `later()`, never reads `_loading` and never bumps `_loadToken`. setBasePixels (open.js 89-135) empties the layers and the undo and bumps `historyGen`, with the comment "a restore still loading must not put the old document over the new image". But setValue never reads `historyGen`: in that comment, "restore" means a queued undo step (history.js 943-1010), not setValue. So nothing stops the restore loop once loadFile has replaced the base.

Entry points with no `_loading` guard:
- the Open button (inpaint_modal.js 93-95)
- Ctrl+drop, or any drop while `width` is still 0 (inpaint_canvas.js 453)
- paste into a tab whose base is not set yet (inpaint_canvas.js 439)
- the node widget's drop (inpaint_ed_chrome.js 40)
- the multi-file open (inpaint_ed_layers.js 31)

Other paths already refuse during a load: host_pictures 401, host_key 127, host_generate 417, host_upscale 249, geometry 628, and openDocument's reuse test (host_documents 280). That shows the intended rule.

There is a second outcome the reviewer did not list. When loadFile's file is small and setValue's own base await (persist 120 / 124) is still pending, setValue's setBasePixels lands after it and silently replaces the picture the user just opened.

Not a known entry. docs/BUGS.md has no load-race entry. verified.json (review_full_2026-11-07) has the related finding that setBasePixels(keepLayers:false) does not reset maps, history, savedSelections and guides after a finished load. That is a different defect (drift in the reset), not this race between setValue and loadFile.

Severity stays should, not must: the window is the seconds of a large restore, the user is replacing that document on purpose, and the mixed layers are visible (they can be deleted). But the tab's autosave then stores the mixed document.

The fix direction is right, with one correction. Bump `_loadToken` in loadFile (or in its callers), not inside setBasePixels: setValue calls setBasePixels itself, so a bump there would end its own restore. Refusing loadFile while `_loading` is set ("the document is still loading"), as host_pictures 401 does, is the simpler option.

findings.claim: The .abr reader moves to the next block with `r.pos = (r.pos + len + 3) & ~3`, where len is an unchecked u32 from the file. The bitwise AND truncates the sum to int32, so a large len can wrap to a position at or before the current one. The `while (r.pos + 12 <= r.length)` loop then reads the same header again and never ends. sampled() (line 142, `pos = (r.pos + len + 3) & ~3`) has the same wrap.
findings.scenario: A brush pack downloaded from the web (or any crafted file): 6.2 header, then `8BIMsamp` with len 4294967281 at offset 12. 16 + len + 3 = 2^32 + 4, ToInt32 gives 4, so the loop goes back to offset 4 forever. Brush tip > Import runs readAbr synchronously on the window, which hangs for good. Autosave also runs in the window, so every edit since the last autosave is lost when the user kills the app. I ran this: a 32-byte buffer with those values made readAbr run until a 5 s timeout killed it.
findings.evidence: inpaint_brushes.js blocks() 121-132: `const len = r.u32(); ... r.pos = (r.pos + len + 3) & ~3;` has no bound against r.length and no check that the position grows. sampled() 138-142 does the same with `pos`. readAbr 287-298 is called from TipsPart.tipsFromAbr (inpaint_ed_tips.js:134) <- importBrushFiles (110), which runs from the tip file input (inpaint_modal.js:168). A Node run of the copied module on that buffer did not return (exit 124 from `timeout 5`).
findings.fix: Compute the next offset in plain arithmetic: `const next = r.pos + len; if (len > r.length - r.pos) break; r.pos = next + ((4 - (next & 3)) & 3);`. Equivalently, break whenever the new position is not greater than the old one or lies past the end. Do the same in sampled(). A test with the crafted header would hold it.
findings.why:
I read renderer/editor/inpaint_brushes.js. In blocks() (lines 122-132) the 12-byte header is read with tag(), tag() and u32(). Each of those calls need(), but need() only checks the bytes about to be read. The next line, `r.pos = (r.pos + len + 3) & ~3`, uses the file's u32 len with no bound, and the bitwise AND applies ToInt32 to the sum.

Two cases follow:
- **Sum in [2^31, 2^32):** pos goes negative. tag() passes need() because a negative pos plus 4 is not past the length, then the next u32's DataView.getUint32 throws a RangeError, so readAbr just fails.
- **Sum in [2^32, 2^32 + pos]:** pos wraps to a small offset at or before the current one. The loop condition `r.pos + 12 <= r.length` stays true and the same headers repeat forever.

The reviewer's numbers are right: header at 4, len read at 12, so pos is 16; 16 + 4294967281 + 3 = 2^32 + 4, and ToInt32 then `& ~3` gives 4. The leading u16/u16 must read 6 or 10 and 1 or 2 so readAbr (line 294) takes readV6, which calls blocks() first (line 256). sampled() (lines 135-158) has the same wrap at line 142: `continue` and the catch's `break` both depend on pos, and a wrapped pos below `end` cycles the same way.

The call path is synchronous on the window: inpaint_ed_tips.js:115 importBrushFiles awaits tipsFromAbr, which calls readAbr(await file.arrayBuffer()) at line 134. A try/catch there cannot stop an endless loop. Nothing in the file guards against a position that does not grow.

I found no entry for this in BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for abr / inpaint_brushes found nothing).

Why should and not must: the window of len values that wrap is only about pos bytes wide near 2^32, so a merely truncated or garbled pack almost never hits it. A crafted brush pack from the web does, and the window hangs until the user kills it, losing the edits since the last autosave. That is a hang a user can hit, not a security hole beyond denial of service.

The fix direction is right: stop when len is greater than r.length - r.pos (or when the new pos is not greater than the old one) in both blocks() and sampled(), using plain arithmetic instead of `& ~3`.

findings.claim: bucketFill awaits floodRegion (pool composite, the coarse settle, the fine flood) and only then pushes its undo step and writes. It is not wrapped in trackEdit, so an undo pressed during the flood is not held back. It undoes the step below. The fill's push then clears the redo stack, and the undone edit is gone for good. The fill also writes into `layer`, read before the await, even when that layer has been removed meanwhile.
findings.scenario: 15000 x 10000 document. Paint a stroke, click with the bucket on a large region (the flood takes up to about 2 s at 15k, per K0b), and press Ctrl+Z before it lands. historyStepNow finds no pending edit and undoes the stroke, which goes onto redo. The fill then lands, pushUndoSnapshot releases every redo step, and the stroke can never be redone. If the active layer is deleted during the flood instead (Delete, an agent's remove_layer), the fill goes into the detached layer, the status says "Filled N px", and an undo step for a missing layer is pushed, which clears redo too.
findings.evidence: onPointerDown (inpaint_ed_pointer.js:427) calls `this.bucketFill(ix, iy)` untracked. bucketFill 292-318: `let layer = this.activeLayer()` happens before `await this.floodRegion(...)` (304), then `pushUndoSnapshot(this.snapshotRect(layer, ...))` (318) and the write. pushUndoSnapshot (inpaint_ed_history.js 431-432) releases and clears this.redo. historyStepNow (992) waits only for `_pendingEdits`, which trackEdit (957) fills. Other async edits are tracked (extend, crop, heal, liquify, feather) for this exact reason, per the comment at inpaint_ed_geometry.js 1477-1482.
findings.fix: Return `this.trackEdit(this.bucketFillNow(ix, iy))`. After the await, check that `layer` is still in this.layers (and is still the active layer) and that historyGen has not moved, and refuse with a status line otherwise. wandSelect in inpaint_ed_select.js has the same untracked await.
findings.why:
I read the code and the race is real. A bucket click goes from onPointerDown (inpaint_ed_pointer.js:427) to `this.bucketFill(ix, iy)` with no trackEdit around it and no `this.pointer` set. bucketFill (inpaint_ed_shape.js:292-318) reads `layer = this.activeLayer()` and then awaits `floodRegion` at line 304. floodRegion awaits holdStack, sampleRegionSettled, the coarse floodShape and up to 8 fine rounds. Only after that does it call `pushUndoSnapshot(..., { label: "Bucket fill" })` without `tracked`, at line 318.

Nothing holds Ctrl+Z back while that runs:
- The document key handler (inpaint_canvas.js:332) only holds keys for `this.pointer.healing`.
- onKey's Ctrl+Z (pointer.js:201) calls undoStep at once.
- historyStepNow (history.js:984-1014) waits only for `_pendingEdits`, which only trackEdit fills. The bucket is not in it.
- `gestureHeld()` is false because the bucket sets no pointer.
- The gen check passes because the fill has not pushed yet.

So the undo takes back the step below, for example a stroke, and pushes it onto redo. Then the fill's pushUndoSnapshot (history.js:431-432) releases and clears `this.redo`, and the stroke can no longer be redone.

After the await nothing checks that `layer` is still in `this.layers`. Only the tile-shape check at 310 runs, and it does not cover a removed layer. So the fill writes into a detached layer, which the removal's undo step may still hold, and it pushes a step for that layer.

Other async edits are wrapped in trackEdit for exactly this reason: feather, grow and invert in inpaint_ed_select.js:1130/1389/1437, and extend, crop, resize, flatten and mergeDown. wandSelect (select.js:1116-1127) has the same untracked await. BUGS.md lists the bucket only in performance rows, and neither verified.json has this; the bucket's only entry there is the unrelated text-layer finding.

Severity is should, not must. A rare timing window loses one redoable edit, or puts a fill into a removed layer. The user's pixels on the canvas stay intact.

The fix direction is right: trackEdit, or a re-check of the layer and historyGen after the await. One caveat: with trackEdit the fill's push should pass `tracked: true`, as the other tracked edits do.

findings.claim: The text panel's textarea and both colour inputs take a `_textUndo` snapshot on focus, and only on focus when none is held. They push it only on `change`. Nothing drops it when the field loses focus without a change, or when renderLayers rebuilds the panel under it. The next edit through the field then pushes this old snapshot. It holds the layer's text, pixels and x / y / w / h from when the field was first focused, so its undo also takes back every edit made in between.
findings.scenario: Click into a text layer's text field and click out without typing (no change event, so `_textUndo` stays). Move the text layer with the text tool, or press Bold, or change its size; each of these pushes its own step. Click the field again (begin keeps the stale snapshot), type a letter, and click out: "Edit text" is pushed with the first snapshot. Ctrl+Z on "Edit text" puts the layer back to its old place, size and style along with the text. The next Ctrl+Z ("Move layer" / "Bold") then shows no change. The same happens when a landing result's renderLayers removes the field while typing: the typing gets no step of its own until the next commit.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_text.js 232: `begin = () => { if (!layer._textUndo) layer._textUndo = this.snapshot({ kind: "text", id: layer.id }); }`. 233: commit runs only from the `change` listeners (244, 269, 298). The focus listeners are at 242, 267 and 296. There is no blur handler. change() (234) pushes its own step without touching `_textUndo`. A text snapshot holds x, y, w, h and px (inpaint_ed_history.js 404), and its restore assigns them back (805-818).
findings.fix: Drop the snapshot when the field loses focus without a change (release it on blur when the value equals the snapshot's), or take a fresh one on every focus and release the old one. Also commit or release a held `_textUndo` before change(), a move or a transform pushes its own step on that layer.
findings.why: Read renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js 228-310. `begin` (232) takes a `kind:"text"` snapshot on focus only when `layer._textUndo` is empty. `commit` (233) pushes it and clears it, but only from the `change` listeners (244, 269, 298). The textarea, colour and outline-colour inputs have no blur handler. `change()` (234) pushes its own step and never touches `_textUndo`. A grep for `_textUndo` finds it cleared in only four kinds of place: releaseDroppedEdits (history 131, a layer an undo took out of the document), distort/warp to pixels (geometry 172), a canvas turn or straighten (geometry 691 and 1050), and setTextAngle (text 182). Nothing clears it for Bold, Italic, size, font, alignment, a move with the text tool, or a panel rebuild. pushUndoSnapshot's flushPendingDebounces handles only `_flushNudge` / `_flushWheel` (history 930-940). The text snapshot holds the text object, pixels and x/y/w/h (history 404), and its restore writes all of them back (history 805-818). So the scenario holds: focus the field and leave it without typing (Chromium fires no change), then Bold or move the layer (each pushes its own step), then focus again (the old snapshot is kept), type and blur. The push is "Edit text" with the first snapshot, so its undo also takes back the Bold and the move, and the next undo step changes nothing. Redo gets the state back, so nothing is lost for good: should, not must. A small side effect: an abandoned snapshot keeps its pixel copy and undo-budget bytes until the next commit. Not in BUGS.md and not in either verified.json (grep for _textUndo / buildTextControls: no hits). The fix direction is right: release the snapshot on blur when nothing changed, or commit/release a held `_textUndo` inside `change()` and before other steps that push on that layer.

findings.claim: Several gestures push their undo step at the press and never take it back when the gesture changes nothing. pushUndoSnapshot clears the redo stack each time. The cases are a plain click on a text layer with the text tool, a click on a layer or handle with the transform tool, a rect/ellipse click in add/subtract mode, and a gradient or rectangle/ellipse shape click without a drag. For the last two, commitStroke pushes the step before it checks that the stroke buffer is empty.
findings.scenario: Paint a stroke, press Ctrl+Z, then click once on a text layer with the text tool to select it, or click the layer with T. A "Move layer" step is pushed, the stroke's redo is released, and Ctrl+Y can no longer bring the stroke back. The history fills with steps that do nothing, and with the default 30-step depth they evict real ones.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_pointer.js 604: `this.pushUndo({ kind: "transform", id: hit.id, label: "Move layer" })` on every text-layer press. 590: the same for transform move/scale. 387 rect/ellipse: pushUndo at the press, and at 973 a click in non-replace mode returns with nothing changed. onPointerUp 1096-1103 never removes the step for an unmoved move/scale. inpaint_ed_strokes.js commitStroke 439-440: `pushUndoSnapshot(this.strokeUndo(p, target), ...)` comes before `if (!p.stroke || p.stroke.empty) return;`. A gradient click never calls gradientDab, and a shape click never calls shapeDab. pushUndoSnapshot (inpaint_ed_history.js 431-432) releases and clears redo.
findings.fix: Take the snapshot at the press but push it only when the gesture changed something. Move/scale/text move: compare x/y/w/h at release with p.orig. Rect click: compare the mode. In commitStroke, return before the push when the buffer is empty. Or keep pushing at the press and drop the step again at release when nothing changed.
findings.why:
I read the code at ce4415ec and the finding holds. pushUndo (inpaint_ed_history.js 411-414) calls pushUndoSnapshot, and pushUndoSnapshot (422-440) releases and clears this.redo on every push. Nothing merges or drops a step that changed nothing. The cases:

(1) Text tool, inpaint_ed_pointer.js 604: a single click on an unlocked text layer pushes a "Move layer" transform step at the press.

(2) Transform tool, 590 for one layer and 572 for a group: a "Move layer" / "Scale" step is pushed at the press. The release branch for move/scale (1096-1103) only refreshes the UI and never compares the position with p.orig, so a click with no drag keeps the step.

(3) Rect/ellipse, 387: the step is pushed at the press. On release, a click without a drag in a mode other than replace returns early (973) and changes nothing. In replace mode the click deselects, so that case is a real change.

(4) Gradient, 523-532: the press only builds the pointer. gradientDab runs only on a move (763). A release with no drag goes to commitLayerPaint and then commitStroke (inpaint_ed_strokes.js 439), which pushes strokeUndo before the `if (!p.stroke || p.stroke.empty) return` check. p.bounds is unset, so strokeRect returns null and strokeUndo snapshots the whole layer (history.js 113-120). A gradient click therefore copies the entire layer into undo, a lot of memory on a 15k layer, and also clears redo. I did not trace the shape path through shapePointerDown, but commitStroke has the same order.

Real use: paint a stroke, press Ctrl+Z, then click a text layer with T or click a layer with the transform tool, and Ctrl+Y no longer brings the stroke back. These no-op steps also take slots from the 30-step depth.

Not known: BUGS.md has no such entry. Neither verified.json lists it; the full review only covers the arrow-key nudge pushing a step per keydown, which is a different path.

The suggested fix direction is right: push only when something changed, or drop the step at release, and in commitStroke return before the push when the buffer is empty. Severity is should. The user loses redo and history depth, and a gradient click costs a whole-layer copy, but no pixels are corrupted.

findings.claim: With the border fill set to noise, extendCanvasNow creates an ImageData of the whole new canvas and fills every pixel with Math.random in a JS loop on the window. It then draws the picture over most of it. Only the added border needs noise.
findings.scenario: 15000 x 10000 picture, extend by 512 px on each side, fill set to noise. The new canvas is 16024 x 11024 = 177 MP. createImageData allocates 707 MB, the loop runs 177 M iterations with three Math.random calls each, and putImageData uploads it all. That is several seconds of a blocked window and a 0.7 GB spike (the time is inferred), all before the upload, while about 15 % of those pixels stay visible.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_geometry.js 1518-1522: `const img = ctx.createImageData(nw, nh); for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) { d[i] = Math.random() * 255; ... } ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);`, followed by `ctx.drawImage(flat, left, top)` at 1537, which covers the inner W x H.
findings.fix: Fill only the four border rectangles (top/bottom bands of nw x top and nw x bottom, left/right bands of left x H and right x H), each with its own small ImageData. Or tile one noise ImageData of a few hundred px with createPattern and fillRect the border.
findings.why: I read extendCanvasNow at inpaint_ed_geometry.js 1485-1572. The "noise" fill is one of the six choices offered in the Canvas tool (inpaint_modal.js 856) and is kept in cropSettings.extendFill. Nothing guards that path and nothing returns early before it. Lines 1519-1522 create an ImageData of the full nw x nh, fill every pixel with three Math.random calls in a synchronous loop on the window, and then putImageData the whole buffer. Line 1537 then draws `flat` at (left, top) and covers the inner W x H, so only the border needs noise. The "stretch edges" branch above it already fills just the border rectangles. I timed the same loop in Node at 16024 x 11024: 2,853 ms for the loop alone. On top of that comes the 707 MB Uint8ClampedArray, which sits beside the full-size `flat` and `nb` canvases this function already holds, plus a full-canvas putImageData. That is about 3 s or more of blocked window and a 0.7 GB spike on a 15k document, about 85 % of it wasted when extending by 512 px. Neither docs/BUGS.md nor the two verified.json files list it. The extend entry in review_full verified.json is the upload race, a different defect. The suggested fix is right: noise only the four border rects, or fillRect them with a small tiled noise pattern from createPattern.

findings.claim: In intersect mode the band jobs (and the window loop) write the complement of the object (invert: a = 255 where the logit is <= 0), so unionBounds is the box of the complement. selectLogits then sets the exact cached bounds to old ∩ complement-bounds. When the object fills whole rows or columns of the processed region (an object touching the picture's edge across its width), the complement does not reach those rows. The cached bounds then exclude selected pixels.
findings.scenario: Ctrl+A, then Object tool Shift+Alt+click the sky of a landscape whose top rows are all sky (or select_point with mode intersect). minGy stays 0 and the processed columns cover the whole width. The complement's first row is the first row with a non-sky pixel, say y = 400, so cachedBounds = [0, 400, W, ...] with selectionDirty false. Rows 0..399 are selected (the ants show them) but lie outside getBounds(). Everything that trusts getBounds then misses that strip: cropRect / planFrame (the Boxes frame, areaHint, prompt context), Each area's count box (countNow reads only b), grow and feather (selectionOverTiles / selectionInWorker work only in bounds ± halo), copySelection's box, patchExtent, and on the canvas backend at large sizes the run's own selection window (stitch.js selectionWindowBox uses getBounds when W*H > SEL_WINDOW_PIXELS). A paid Generate on that selection can inpaint only part of it.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_select.js 721 jobInvert = (mode === 'intersect'); 734-751 band jobs with invert; 761-770 unionBounds from bRes.bounds; inpaint_worker.js 1840-1849: a = inside ? (invert ? 0 : 255) : (invert ? 255 : 0), and the bounds collect a > 0, i.e. the complement; the canvas loop at 796-806 does the same. 838-842: hint = [max(old0,u0), max(old1,u1), min(old2,u2), min(old3,u3)]. 850 markSelectionChanged(hint) -> 1474-1476 cachedBounds = hint, selectionDirty = false (exact, never rescanned; getBounds 527-534 in inpaint_ed_export.js returns it as is). selectRange gets this right for the same mode: 576 hint = { within: oldBounds }.
findings.fix: For intersect pass { within: oldBounds } (or { within: old ∩ boundsBox }) as selectRange does, so getBounds rescans inside it; never use the complement's bounds as the result's.
findings.why: I read renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js 673-850. In intersect mode the selection is first cut to boundsBox (717-719). The bands then run with jobInvert=true and bandMode "subtract" (721-722). The worker (inpaint_worker.js ~1840) and the window loop (796-806) both write a=255 for pixels outside the object and collect bounds over a>0, so unionBounds is the box of the complement inside the band rows. At 838-842 the hint is old ∩ unionBounds, and markSelectionChanged (1468-1477) stores an array hint as exact: selectionDirty=false, loose=false. getBounds (inpaint_ed_export.js 527-534) then hands it back without a rescan. The real result is old ∩ boundsBox ∩ object, and that has no fixed relation to the complement's box. The ±1 grid-cell margin round the object's grid extent (699-702) usually keeps the complement as wide as the object. At the picture edges, though, the margin is clamped away, so an object that spans the box's full width and touches the top or bottom edge (sky over a landscape after Ctrl+A, Shift+Alt+click) leaves its edge rows out of the complement's bounds. The cached bounds then miss selected rows. Callers reach this: host_helpers.js 469/501 pass the user's mode, and select_point with mode intersect does too. selectRange covers the same case correctly with { within: oldBounds } (576-578). Neither BUGS.md nor the two verified.json files list it. verified.json:685 is a different selectLogits defect: the layer clip in the window loop. The fix is right: pass { within: old ∩ boundsBox }, or { within: oldBounds }, so getBounds rescans inside a superset. It is a should, not a must, because the ants show the full selection and only consumers of getBounds (crop, grow and feather, Each area) go wrong.

findings.claim: The in-app background removal awaits host.cutoutInApp (seconds: BiRefNet on CPU measured 4.8 s in U0, longer on the first load) and then applies the mask to pending.layer, the object captured at the click, with no check that it is still the document's layer. The ComfyUI path checks this (applyCutoutFile 93: this.layers.includes(layer)). An undo or redo of any 'layers' step rebuilds every layer object with the same ids. pushUndo then snapshots the live copy, clearing the redo stack, and the mask goes onto the detached object.
findings.scenario: Rename layer B (a 'layers' step), click Cutout on layer A with an in-app model, then press Ctrl+Z to undo the rename while the model runs. applySnapshot (inpaint_ed_history.js 574) replaces this.layers with fresh objects. The cutout lands: pushUndo({kind:'mask', id}) finds the new A by id and pushes a 'Remove background' step, which empties this.redo, so the rename's redo is gone. layer.maskPx is written on the old, detached A, so nothing changes on screen. The status still says 'background removed with BiRefNet, 63% kept'. If A was deleted meanwhile, the status claims success too.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_masks.js 60 cutoutPending = { layer, backend }; 63 await host.cutoutInApp(...) then applyCutoutImage(img, this.cutoutPending); 107 const layer = pending.layer; 120 pushUndo({ kind: 'mask', id: layer.id }); 121 layer.maskPx = m (the captured object). inpaint_ed_history.js 387-397 snapshotOf finds the layer by id (the new object); 431-432 pushUndoSnapshot releases and empties redo; 574 a 'layers' restore makes new objects ({ ...l }). historyStepNow (984-993) waits only for _pendingEdits, and cutoutLayer is not tracked. The buildMaskRow busy check (inpaint_ed_layers.js 977) is by identity too, so after the restore the row no longer shows the cutout as running.
findings.fix: In applyCutoutImage look the layer up again by id (this.layers.find(l => l.id === pending.layer.id)). Refuse with a status line when it is gone, or when its px is not the one the input was read from. Write the mask to that live object. Or trackEdit the cutout so an undo waits for it.
findings.why: I read the code and the path runs as the finding says. cutoutLayer (inpaint_ed_masks.js:60-63) stores `{ layer, backend }` and then awaits host.cutoutInApp. That call (host_helpers.js:385-402) awaits cutoutInput and then helperCall("cutout"), which takes seconds. Then applyCutoutImage(img, this.cutoutPending) uses `pending.layer` (line 107), the object captured at the click. It never re-checks that the object is still in this.layers. The ComfyUI route's applyCutoutFile does check (`this.layers.includes(layer)`, line 93). Nothing stops an undo in the meantime. undoStep/historyStepNow (inpaint_ed_history.js 943-1040) wait only for `_pendingEdits`, and the cutout is never passed to trackEdit. The only busy check on the history path is turnBlocked, and that applies only to 'canvas' / 'turn' steps. cutoutPending is checked only by generate, upscale and the geometry block. A 'layers' undo or redo then runs applySnapshot (574-578), which rebuilds every layer as `installLayerAliases({ ...l })` from snapshotLayer's shallow copies (174-175). When the cutout lands, pushUndo({kind:'mask', id}) goes through snapshot(), which looks the layer up by id (387) and so finds the new object. pushUndoSnapshot then empties this.redo (430-432). After that, `layer.maskPx = m` is written to the detached old object, so nothing shows on screen. The status line still reads "background removed with ..., N% kept". If the layer was deleted during the run, snapshot() returns null and the push is skipped. The mask still goes onto the detached object and the status still claims success. The result is a lost, possibly slow helper run, a false success line, and a lost redo step. No existing pixels are lost, so this is should, not must. The issue is not in BUGS.md or in either verified.json (the cutout entries there are about the main-process block and memory). The fix direction is right: in applyCutoutImage, look the layer up again by id (and refuse if it is gone, or if its px changed), or wrap the in-app cutout in trackEdit so an undo waits for it. The anchor fits line 107 (`const layer = pending.layer`) better than 63.

findings.claim: A selection by text on the user's ComfyUI applies its mask on the window through several document-size buffers at once. It decodes the mask into a W x H canvas, reads it back whole, builds a second W x H canvas and ImageData, and draws that into the whole selection. In layer mode, layerAlpha adds another document-size canvas, readback and array. All of it is synchronous.
findings.scenario: 15000 x 10000 document, Select by text 'shirt' with SAM3 on ComfyUI. The answer's PNG goes into tmp (a 600 MB canvas), getImageData (600 MB), then shape (600 MB canvas) with createImageData (600 MB) and putImageData. sel.drawInto(null, ...) then draws the whole document canvas into the selection. With Source = active layer, layerAlpha adds a 600 MB canvas, a 600 MB readback and a 150 MB Uint8Array. That is about 2.4-3.2 GB of transient memory and seconds of blocked window per select by text, for a mask that usually covers a small part of the picture. Above Chromium's canvas limit makeCanvas throws, and the result is lost after the run.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_segment.js 499-502 tmp = makeCanvas(this.width, this.height); drawImage; getImageData(0,0,W,H); 503 clip = layerAlpha(pending.layer) (146-153: makeCanvas W x H, getImageData, Uint8Array W*H); 504-514 shape = makeCanvas(W,H), createImageData(W,H), a JS loop over every pixel, putImageData; 517-520 sel.drawInto(null, ...) over the whole picture. Not among BUGS.md's object-shape entry (objectShape) or review finding canvas-c/F8 (maskToCanvas on the run path).
findings.fix: Read the mask's bounds first (a coarse pass or the decoded image in bands), then build the shape only over that box and combine it with sel.combine(bytesSource(...)) per band, as selectRange and selectLogits do. Clip by the layer's box only (storeRows of the layer, or layerAlpha over the box).
findings.why:
I read renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_segment.js 493-531 at ce4415ec, and the code matches the claim. applyMaskFile runs makeCanvas(W,H) for tmp and drawImage scaled to the document size, then getImageData of the whole document. With pending.layer set it calls layerAlpha (146-153), which adds another W x H canvas, a readback and a W*H Uint8Array. It then makes a second W x H canvas, createImageData(W,H), loops in JS over every pixel, calls putImageData, and finishes with sel.drawInto(null, ...) over the whole selection. All of this runs synchronously on the window and has no tile or band path.

The path does run in real use. host.js 208-215 sends every inpaint_mask output whose purpose is neither "segments" nor "cutout" to ed.applyMaskFile. That covers select by text through the ComfyUI helpers. SAM3 is ComfyUI-only by the project's decisions, so text selection has no in-app alternative. No guard or early return skips the full-size work.

At 15000 x 10000 that adds up to several 600 MB buffers per call, plus 150 MB for the layer clip. The sibling selectRange / selectLogits in inpaint_ed_select.js already works in bands and combines them with sel.combine on tiles, so the suggested fix direction fits the code.

It is not a known item:
- BUGS.md's entry near line 195-204 covers objectShape / applySegmentsFile hover shapes.
- review_full canvas-c/F8 covers maskToCanvas on the run path.
- The layerAlpha mentions in verified.json are about storeArgs ignoring scale and mask on tiles, a different defect.
- review_external has no entry for this function.

The severity stays should rather than must. Under Chromium's area cap, 15k still fits, so the mask is not lost in the tuned case; the cost is a long block and a transient spike of several GB. Only a document past the canvas limit makes makeCanvas throw, and then the free local helper's mask is lost but no pixels are.

findings.claim: When the reference labels change (a reference reordered, hidden, deleted, made a reference, merged), refsMutated rewrites the @img tokens of the prompt, the negative, Revert's text, a pending upsample and the registered fields so each token keeps naming its picture by layer id. It never touches the box descriptions. The Boxes plugin (and the node's own boxes) store `desc` with `@img<n>` by label number, and resolve it only at send time against the labels as they are then. So after a renumbering, a box description names another picture.
findings.scenario: Two shown references: A (@img1, a red hat) and B (@img2, a lamp). The user adds a box "the hat from @img1" and writes a prompt with @img1. Then the user moves B above A in the reference list (moveReference -> reorderLayer -> layersRestacked -> refsMutated). The prompt's token becomes @img2 and still names A, but the box desc stays "@img1". At Generate, plugins/boxes descOf -> runDesc (boxes_model.js:242) maps @img1 through the current labels to {@layer:B.id}. The paid FLUX 3 / Ideogram run is told to place the lamp in the hat's box. Hiding A instead leaves the desc's "@img1" naming B, and a desc "@img2" names no layer and goes out as literal text.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_refs.js:78-94 refsMutated computes r = remap(before, target) and applies it to promptText, negativeText and remapOthers. remapOthers (112-123) covers promptBackup, upsamplePending and _remapTargets only. The only addRemapTarget caller is shell_generate.js:444 (the Generate new dialog). plugins/boxes/main.js:57-59 descOf builds a label -> layer id map from doc.layers() labels at send time, and boxes_model.js:242 runDesc replaces /@img(n)/ through it. The stored desc is written once in normaliseBox (boxes_model.js:92) and never remapped. The node reads the same pluginData.boxes desc (inpaint_ed_persist.js:435, promptPayload keeps the @img text), so it drifts the same way.
findings.fix: Remap the box descriptions together with the prompt. In the app, emit an event from refsMutated (or register a remap target from the Boxes plugin) that passes the remap function. The plugin then rewrites every desc and writes the data without an undo step of its own, as the geometry handler does. In the node, call this.boxes from remapOthers. The undo snapshots of plugin data need the same map, as the field's history gets it. Or store desc tokens by layer id ({@layer:id}) at write time and show them as @img<n>. Mind that reftokens parks an unlabelled token as @img?<id>, which boxes_model's TOKEN does not read, so runDesc has to learn that form or refuse it.
findings.why: I read inpaint_ed_refs.js. refsMutated (78-94) builds r = remap(before, target) and applies it to promptText and negativeText (with the field history), then calls remapOthers. remapOthers (112-123) covers promptBackup, upsamplePending and _remapTargets, and nothing else. A grep finds no remap, refsMutated, refMap or addRemapTarget use anywhere in plugins/boxes/, renderer/editor/boxes_*.js or inpaint_boxes.js. The only refsMutated call outside the editor is plugins.js:265, a role change, which goes through the same function. So a stored box desc is never rewritten. At send time plugins/boxes/main.js:57-59 descOf builds a label -> layer id map from doc.layers() as it is then. doc.layers() gives each reference the label "img"+n from ed.refLabels() (commands_util.js:69-70). boxes_model.js:242-243 runDesc then turns @imgN into {@layer:<current id for N>} and leaves an unknown N as literal text. After a reorder, a hide or a delete of a reference, the prompt's tokens follow their layers but a box desc's @img1 points at whichever layer holds label 1 now. That is the wrong picture in the box on a paid FLUX 3 / Ideogram run. The node side does the same: inpaint_ed_persist.js:435-441 sends pluginData.boxes through promptPayload together with the current referenceLabels, so nodes.py resolves the desc tokens against the new numbering too. No BUGS.md entry and no verified.json finding covers box descriptions and ref remapping (grepped). I rate it should, not must: you need @img tokens in a box description plus a reference reorder, hide or delete before the run. The result is a wrong picture placed, with no data loss. The fix direction is right: remap pluginData.boxes descs in remapOthers, or keep them by layer id. The parked @img?<id> form needs handling in runDesc, as the reviewer says.

findings.claim: Copy rows names a From box's picture from its index in shownReferences(doc). That list is doc.layers(): the editor's stack, bottom first. Everywhere else in the same clipboard text, the prompt's and the descriptions' @img<n> become <ref_image_n>, with n the label, which counts from the top. With two or more shown references, a From row's `from` names the other picture than the tokens. The node's copy of this code (inpaint_boxes.js:175-178) uses ed.referenceLayers(), which is top first, so the two hosts differ.
findings.scenario: Shown references: A on top (@img1) and B below it (@img2). A From box places A, and the prompt says "put the cup from @img1 on the table". Copy rows gives an instruction that says <ref_image_1>, while the row says {"from": "ref_image_2", ...}: shownReferences = [B, A], so k = 1 gives ref_image_2. The text the user pastes into another tool places the wrong picture. The panel's From-layer default (refs[0], line 298) is also the bottom reference, the highest label, not @img1.
findings.evidence: plugins/boxes/main.js:40 shownReferences = doc.layers().filter(role reference && visible). plugins.js:65 Document.layers() maps editor.layers in array order. editor.layers is bottom first: inpaint_ed_layers.js:532 pushes a new layer on top, and inpaint_ed_refs.js:18 referenceLayers() reverses the array so that top = reference 1. In copyRows, line 173 maps @img<n> to <ref_image_n> by label, clipDesc does the same (boxes_model.js:249), and line 175 nameOf uses `ref_image_${k + 1}` with k the index in the bottom-first list. shownReferences also keeps a visible reference without pixels (no label), which shifts the indices too.
findings.fix: Name the From picture by its label: nameOf: (id) => { const l = doc.layers().find((x) => x.id === id); return l && l.label ? `ref_image_${l.label.slice(3)}` : null; }. Or build refs as the labelled references sorted by label. Use the same order for the panel's From default and its option list.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. In plugins/boxes/main.js:40, shownReferences(doc) is doc.layers() filtered to role reference and visible. doc.layers() (renderer/plugins.js:65) maps editor.layers in array order, and that order is bottom first: RefsPart.referenceLayers() in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:18 calls .reverse() on that same array, with the comment "top of the list = reference 1". layerSummary (renderer/commands_util.js:70) gives each reference its label "img"+n from ed.refLabels(), which numbers top first. copyRows (main.js:173) rewrites the prompt's @img<n> as <ref_image_n> by label, and clipDesc (boxes_model.js:249) does the same for the descriptions. But nameOf at line 175 returns `ref_image_${k+1}` with k the index in the bottom-first list. Example: references A on top (@img1) and B below (@img2). shownReferences is [B, A], so a From box on A becomes `from: ref_image_2` while the instruction text says <ref_image_1>. The pasted rows place the wrong picture.

shownReferences also keeps a visible reference with no px. referenceLayers drops those (`&& l.px`), so such a layer has no label but still takes an index and shifts the numbers. The node's copy (renderer/editor/inpaint_boxes.js:175-178) uses ed.referenceLayers(), which is top first, so there the numbers agree with the tokens. The two hosts disagree, and the app plugin is the one that is wrong.

Who is affected: the Copy rows button (main.js:238) runs this for anyone with two or more shown references and a From box. The run path is not involved; only the clipboard text is wrong. The From default in the panel, refs[0] at main.js:298, also picks the bottom reference (the highest label) rather than @img1. That is a small UI inconsistency, not wrong data.

Not already known: nothing in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json mentions copyRows, Copy rows or this order.

The proposed fix is right: build nameOf from the layer's label, or use labelled references sorted by label. Severity is should rather than must: it gives a wrong result in a clipboard export and touches no document pixels.

findings.claim: Selection → box (the panel button, the Plugins menu action and the MCP command boxes.from_selection) needs only the selection's bounds. It gets them from doc.selection({ box: true }), which reads the whole bounds rectangle of the selection mask as RGBA ImageData and builds a Uint8Array mask of the same size, then drops both.
findings.scenario: 15000 x 10000 document, Select All (or a large selection), then Selection → box. Document.selection: bounds() is 15000 x 10000, then sel.readRect(0, 0, 15000, 10000) allocates a 600 MB ImageData (inpaint_tiles.js:1397 new ImageData(w, h), then a copy of every tile), and the loop fills a 150 MB Uint8Array. The window freezes for seconds and may hit an out-of-memory error on a 15k document, only to read four numbers. The comment says "not a mask of the whole picture", but the box mask of a select-all is the whole picture.
findings.evidence: plugins/boxes/main.js:161-165 uses only sel.bounds. plugins.js:182-190 selection({ box: true }) calls this.editor.sel.readRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h) and loops over b.w * b.h. commands_util.js:300 bounds(ed) gets the same numbers from ed.getBounds() with no pixel read. cropCheck in the same file (line 98) already calls doc.editor.getBounds().
