findings.why: plugins/boxes/main.js:160-165 `fromSelection` calls `doc.selection({ box: true })` and uses only `sel.bounds` (passed to `selectionInput`, boxes_model.js:149-155, which reads only x/y/w/h). In renderer/plugins.js:182-190 `selection({box:true})` gets the bounds from `bounds(this.editor)`, then always runs `this.editor.sel.readRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h)`. On tiles that is inpaint_tiles.js:1387ff, which allocates `new ImageData(w, h)` and copies every tile. After that it fills a `Uint8Array(b.w*b.h)`. Both are thrown away. Nothing earlier returns before the read and no guard skips it. With Select All on a 15000x10000 document that is a 600 MB ImageData plus a 150 MB array, all to get four numbers. That freezes the window for a long time, and readRect turns a failed allocation into an out-of-memory error. The comment "not a mask of the whole picture" is wrong for a selection as large as the picture. The fix is cheap and already exists. `bounds(ed)` (commands_util.js:300) reads only `ed.getBounds()`. The same Document class has a bounds-only return at plugins.js:207, so fromSelection can use `bounds(doc.editor)` (or a `doc.selectionBounds()` wrapper). plugins/sample/main.js:69 makes the same call; check whether it needs the mask. This is not in BUGS.md or in either verified.json. I rate it should, not must: it costs time and memory, and the user's pixels are not at risk.

findings.claim: The sample plugin is enabled by default. Its colour probe keeps one 256 x 256 ImageData (256 KB) for every 256-px square the cursor has hovered, with no cap. The cache is dropped only on a 'changed' event of that document or when the tool is selected again. Each new square also costs a synchronous exact flatten of its box.
findings.scenario: 15000 x 10000 document, the Probe tool (K) active, the cursor swept over the picture at fit zoom, where one screen pixel is about ten image pixels. Every square entered adds 256 KB. A full sweep reaches 59 x 40 = 2,360 tiles, about 600 MB of ImageData kept in the renderer until the next edit. While the user only hovers, the memory keeps growing, beside the document's own tiles.
findings.evidence: plugins/sample/main.js:12 the module-level probeCache, a Map of tiles. Lines 103-108: tile key, then on a miss doc.flatten({ box, exact: true }).getImageData(...) is stored with probeCache.tiles.set(key, img), with no eviction. Line 122: onSelect clears it. Line 126: the 'changed' event clears it. plugin.json has enabledByDefault: true.
findings.fix: Keep a small LRU, for example the last 16 tiles: delete the oldest key when the Map grows past it. Or keep only the current tile. One pixel read per hover through doc.flatten({ box: [x, y, x + 1, y + 1], exact: true }) is also cheap enough.
findings.why:
I read plugins/sample/main.js at ce4415ec, and the claim holds. Line 12 declares a module-level probeCache = { doc, tiles: Map }. In probe() (lines 98-114), every 256-px square the cursor enters that is not in the cache causes a synchronous doc.flatten({ box, exact: true }).getImageData(...) of up to 256x256 (256 KB). The result is stored with probeCache.tiles.set(key, img) on line 108. There is no size cap and no eviction anywhere.

The cache is dropped only in three cases:
- onSelect (line 122), when the tool is picked again.
- The 'changed' event for the same document (line 126). Hovering emits no 'changed': the probe only calls doc.status.
- A probe on a different doc.id (line 100), which replaces the whole cache.

plugin.json has "enabledByDefault": true and registers the tool on key K, so the path runs in a stock install whenever the user hovers with the Probe.

Size: at 15000 x 10000 there are 59 x 40 = 2,360 squares, so a full sweep holds about 600 MB. At fit zoom one square is roughly 25 screen px, so an ordinary hover over part of the picture still keeps tens to hundreds of MB. All of it sits in the renderer next to the document's own tiles, and it grows until the next edit. A 30k picture would allow four times as much.

No entry in docs/BUGS.md or in either verified.json mentions the probe cache (grepped 'probe'; the hits are about comfy.js probe and AgentBackend). So this is a new finding, not a known one.

The growth is bounded by the picture size and is reset on any edit, which keeps it at should rather than must. The fix direction is right: a small LRU (Map insertion order, delete the first key past about 16 entries), or keep only the current square.

findings.claim: flattenNow takes its undo snapshot and the composite, then awaits the upload: uploadBlob at 761, or flattenToCanvas plus `await uploadCanvas` at 765. After the await it commits without checking compositeVersion or historyGen again. It sets `this.base` to the composite taken earlier and drops every non-control, non-reference layer as it stands now (770). So an edit made, or a layer added, during the upload is in neither the new base nor the undo snapshot.
findings.scenario: Canvas backend, which always takes this path because bandPlan is null without tileMode. Or tiles with a colour-matched layer above a filter, where bandPlan/stackOnly gives null. A 15000 x 10000 document. The user presses Flatten, which takes seconds: a 600 MB canvas flattened, then a worker PNG encode and the upload. During that time the user goes on with a brush stroke on a layer, or a paid Generate / API result lands as a new layer (addResults has no guard against _pendingEdits). The commit replaces the base with the composite made before the stroke or the result, and filters the layers list, which removes the new result layer or the stroked layer. Undo restores `before`, which was taken before both, and the redo state is the flattened one. The stroke, or the paid result layer, is gone from the document.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_composite.js:742-783. 749: `before = this.snapshot({ kind: "canvas" })`. 752-758: encodeComposite. Its `changed()` check covers only the band reads (encodeComposite 624-640). 761: `ref = await uploadBlob(...)`, or 764-766: `flattenToCanvas` then `await uploadCanvas(flat, ...)`, with no version check after. 768-773: `pushed = true; this.pushUndoSnapshot(before, ...); this.layers = this.layers.filter((l) => this.isControl(l) || this.isReference(l)); this.base = { ref, px }`. bandPlan (583) returns null when `!this.tileMode`, so the canvas backend always takes the uploadCanvas path. flatten() only wraps the run in trackEdit (inpaint_ed_history.js:957), which orders undo/redo and blocks no edits. The same class is in verified.json for crop/resize/extend (canvas-a, 'cropCanvasNow ... never re-checks'). Flatten is not listed there, and turnDocumentNow is the model for the recheck.
findings.fix: Do what turnDocumentNow does. Record `const gen = this.historyGen, ver = this.compositeVersion` (and the layer ids) before the encode. After the upload, if either moved or a gesture is held, release `before` and `px`, and refuse with a status line ('the picture changed while it was flattened; try again'). Or flatten again from the new state. Alternatively set a busy flag that addResults and the stroke start respect while the upload runs.
findings.why:
I read inpaint_ed_composite.js:742-787. flattenNow takes `before = this.snapshot({kind:"canvas"})` at 749. On tiles that snapshot holds copy-on-write clones, so later writes do not reach it (inpaint_ed_history.js:374). It then awaits encodeComposite (relightSettled, stackSource, the band encode), and after that `uploadBlob` (761) or `flattenToCanvas` plus `await uploadCanvas` (764-765). After the await it commits without any check: it pushes `before`, filters `this.layers` down to control and reference layers as they are now (770), and sets the base to the composite it took earlier.

encodeComposite's `changed()` check (647-667) covers only the band reads. It does not cover the upload after them, and the canvas path (bandPlan is null without tileMode, 583) has no check at all. Nothing blocks input during that window. flatten() only wraps the run in trackEdit (history.js:957-963), which orders undo and redo. onPointerDown (inpaint_ed_pointer.js:319ff) refuses only a held heal or a liquify stroke. Flatten sets no `_turning`-style flag. turnDocumentNow (geometry.js:658-668) shows the recheck this function lacks: historyGen, basePx, size, gestureHeld.

So the reviewer's scenario holds. A result layer that addResults lands during the upload, or a stroke on a layer, is dropped by the filter, and it is not in `before` either. Undo of the Flatten restores the state before it, and undoing the edit's own step after that gives back the same earlier state, so the paid result or the stroke cannot be recovered.

It is not a repeat. review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:321 names cropCanvasNow, resizeImageNow and extendCanvasNow for this class but not flattenNow, and BUGS.md has no flatten entry. mergeDownNow's merge into the base (inpaint_ed_layers.js:356-373) has the same gap and is worth fixing with it.

Severity stays should, as for the listed crop/resize/extend race. The window is the upload's second or two at 15k, and seconds on the canvas backend. The likely way to hit it is a run already in flight landing while Flatten uploads. The fix direction is right: copy turnDocumentNow's historyGen / compositeVersion / gestureHeld recheck, release `before` and `px`, and refuse with a status line.

findings.function: applyBlur (and the plugins' blur() in plugins/effects/common.js:153 and plugins/film/common.js:155)
findings.claim: After the blur, applyBlur draws the unblurred source behind the result with destination-over, so that the edge fringe stays opaque. On any half-transparent pixel this composites the source under the blurred copy. The result's alpha becomes a_blur + a_src * (1 - a_blur) instead of the blurred alpha, and colours mix with the unblurred source. The effects pack's Glass frost uses the same blur() on its whole input.
findings.scenario: A transparent document: a cutout or a transparent Generate-new result with soft edges or a uniformly 50 % transparent area. Add a Gaussian blur filter layer. A uniform alpha-128 area comes out at alpha 192, although the blur of a constant must keep it. Inside the silhouette the edge stays hard: there the opaque source is backed in, while the halo spreads outward only. Since the plain-filter fix (clearRect before the draw), this result replaces the input on screen and, through the same applyBlur, in the tiles program's exports. Glass with Frost > 0 on such a picture raises its alpha the same way.
findings.evidence: inpaint_filters.js:925-952: mirrored padding, `octx.filter = blur`, then :948-950 `globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-over'; drawImage(src)`. Porter-Duff destination-over gives a_out = a_dst + a_src (1 - a_dst). applyFilterLayer :1337 clears and replaces for a plain layer. The blur filter has no GL path (not in SUPPORTED, no PLUGIN_GL entry), so bands use this code too (applyFilter :1447). plugins/effects/glass.js:376 uses `blur(src, frostPx)` as the working source, with common.js:153-156 using the same backing.
findings.fix: Back the fringe only where it is needed. The mirrored pad already covers 3 sigma, so either drop the destination-over, or restore exactly the source alpha. Alternatively, apply the backing only when the source is opaque (or only to the outer rows and columns when pad < 3 sigma because W or H is small). Add a pixels-gate case: an identity-size blur over a uniform alpha-128 layer must stay at 128.
findings.why:
I read inpaint_filters.js:925-953. applyBlur pads the canvas with mirrored strips, blurs it, and then at :948-950 draws the unblurred `src` under the result with `destination-over`. The doc comment says why: the fringe is "backed with the source so alpha stays 255". That only holds for an opaque input. Porter-Duff destination-over gives a_out = a_blur + a_src(1 - a_blur), so a uniform alpha-128 area comes out at about 192, and its colour is mixed with the unblurred source. Inside an opaque cutout the inner edge stays at 255, so only the outer halo softens.

The path does run. Blur is not in the GL SUPPORTED set (inpaint_filters_gl.js:143), so applyFilter (:1440-1449) always falls through to f.apply = applyBlur. The input to a filter layer is the composite below it (`ctx.canvas`/chain surface in inpaint_ed_filters.js applyFilterLayer), and in a transparent document that composite is transparent. Since the fix of the must filters/filter-layer-over-its-own-input, a plain layer does `clearRect` and then draws the result (:~1372), so the raised alpha is exactly what lands on screen and in exports. That earlier fix solved the double composite in applyFilterLayer; this backing is a separate step inside the filter's own apply, so it does not repeat that entry. Nothing in BUGS.md or either verified.json mentions the blur backing.

The plugins' blur() has the same backing: plugins/effects/common.js:153-156 and plugins/film/common.js:133-156. Glass frost uses it (glass.js:376), and so do the film filters at filters.js:187, :427 and :449. The fix direction is right: the mirrored pad already covers 3 sigma when W and H allow it, so the backing is only needed where pad was capped by min(W, H), or it should restore the source alpha exactly. The defect is a wrong result on transparent documents only and the layer is non-destructive, so it is a should, not a must.

findings.claim: relightWhole keeps the relight filter layer object it was handed. After the generative route answers, it hides that object and writes its params on it. If the user undoes or redoes a "layers" step while the run waits, applySnapshot replaces every layer object with a copy. The live relight layer then stays visible above the new relit pixel layer, so the relight is applied twice on screen and in exports, after a paid run.
findings.scenario: The user adds a relight filter layer and places lights, then runs Relight via Magnific / fal / Comfy Cloud (tens of seconds, paid). While it waits they press Ctrl+Z or Ctrl+Shift+Z on any "layers" step (an add, delete, duplicate or restack; undo is not blocked by providerPending). The editor's layers become copies. On landing, `layer.visible = false` (352), `layer.params = {...}` (354) and `markFilterChanged(layer)` (358) hit the detached object. The new "Relight (magnific)" layer lands under the still-visible relight filter. The in-app shader then relights the already relit pixels, and the undo step just pushed records that state. The status line says the filter layer was hidden.
findings.evidence: host_relight.js:25 relightWhole(editor, layer, ...) never finds the layer again by id. Between 61 and 352 it awaits relightSettled, encodeComposite, relightSend / comfyPictureRun (177, 246), bytesToImage, the relight_ratio pool job and uploadResult. inpaint_ed_history.js:570-575 applySnapshot for kind "layers" sets `this.layers = snap.layers.map((l) => installLayerAliases({ ...l, ... }))`, so every layer is a new object. historyStepNow (984-1020) refuses only canvas / turn steps while turnBlocked, not layers steps. host_key.js:709-711 landKey fixes exactly this pattern for the key ("an undo or redo of a layers step meanwhile rebuilds every layer object ... `live = (l) => editor.layers.find((x) => x.id === l.id)`"). The relight landing has no such lookup. readSig's `l === layer` exclusion (48) also stops matching after the swap.
findings.fix: Before the landing (after the size check at ~327), look the layer up again: `const live = editor.layers.find((x) => x.id === layer.id) || null;`. Use `live` for `visible = false`, `params.last` and markFilterChanged, and skip hiding when it was deleted. In readSig compare by id (`l.id === layer.id`) rather than identity. Restoring `wasVis` after the read (89-91) has the same issue on a smaller window: restore by id there too.
findings.why:
I read host_relight.js relightWhole from start to end. It holds the `layer` argument for the whole run and never looks it up again by id. On landing it sets `layer.visible = false` (352), sets `layer.params = {...}` (354) and calls `editor.markFilterChanged(layer)` (358), all on that same object. Before that it awaits encodeComposite, relightSend or comfyPictureRun (up to 300 s), bytesToImage, the relight_ratio pool job and uploadResult.

Undo is not blocked during a provider run. undoStep (inpaint_ed_history.js:943) queues historyStepNow, and historyStepNow (984-1020) refuses only canvas and turn steps while turnBlocked(). It never checks providerPending, and no undo entry point (pointer.js:201, modal.js:321) does either. applySnapshot for kind "layers" (570-575) sets `this.layers = snap.layers.map((l) => installLayerAliases({ ...l, ... }))`, so every layer becomes a new object. After any layers undo or redo during the wait, the editor's live relight filter layer is a copy, and the hide hits the detached original. The new "Relight (route)" pixel layer then lands under a relight filter that is still visible, so the light is applied twice on screen and in exports, after a paid run. The pushUndo at 330 records that doubled state, and the status line still says the filter layer was hidden.

Side effect: readSig's `l === layer` exclusion (48) no longer matches the copy, so `changed` comes out true for no real change.

host_key.js:709-711 landKey already fixes this exact pattern with a by-id lookup (`live = (l) => editor.layers.find((x) => x.id === l.id)`), which confirms that the rebuild happens and that this fix is the right direction. Not listed in docs/BUGS.md or in either verified.json; the only relightWhole mentions there are about recipe-id lookups.

Severity is should, not must: nothing is lost, the user can hide the filter layer by hand, but the result after a paid run is wrong.

findings.claim: settleKey treats whatever the document holds after its flushEditor await as the saved file's state. An edit the user makes while that await is still running (the selection's re-encode, the layer syncs, the _restoring wait) gets its hash written into docFile.key. The tab then shows clean although the .scumble file does not hold that edit, so closing the tab asks nothing.
findings.scenario: The user opens a 15k .scumble that has a selection, or restarts the app with such a tab restored clean (docFile.clean). setValue re-encodes the selection in the background, which takes a few seconds, and flushEditor (lines 37-45) waits up to 60 s for it. While it waits the user paints a stroke. flushEditor's edited() loop (line 36) uploads the stroke, line 89 hashes getValue() with the stroke in it, and line 91 stores that hash as docFile.key because the key is still null (open) or clean is set (restore). documentDirty (lines 69-77) now finds _stateKey equal to docFile.key, so the tab has no '*'. shell.js:297 closeDocument asks to save only when documentDirty is true, so Ctrl+W closes the tab without asking. The file on disk never gets the stroke; only Reopen Closed Tab can bring it back. A later Ctrl+S on that tab also looks unneeded, because the tab says it is saved.
findings.evidence: host_documents.js settleKey 84-94: `await this.flushEditor(ed, () => {}, "saving")` (87), then `const key = hashString(ed.getValue())` (89) and `if (!ed.docFile.key || ed.docFile.clean) ed.docFile.key = key` (91), with no check that the user changed the document during the await. It is called from openDocument at line 288 after restore() and shell.activate(ed) (286), so the tab is already live and editable. host_setup.js:248 calls it without awaiting it after a session restore, for every tab whose docFile is set. flushEditor 29-46 waits for _restoring (31), heldEdit (32), the pointer (33), up to three syncLayers rounds (36) and the selection encode for up to 60 s (38-45). On a large selection the encode runs in the background (inpaint_ed_persist.js getValue 21-30, encodeSelectionSoon), so the wait lasts seconds. documentDirty 69-77 compares only _stateKey with docFile.key once nothing is dirty or unencoded.
findings.fix: Take a change mark before the await, for example `const top0 = ed.undo[ed.undo.length - 1], n0 = ed.undo.length, gen0 = ed.historyGen`. After flushEditor, if any of these moved, the user changed the tab during the settle: set `ed._stateKey = key` but do not adopt it as docFile.key. Leave docFile.key as the file's key, or keep it null so documentDirty stays true, and drop `clean`. Adopt the key only when nothing moved.
findings.why:
I read the code at ce4415ec and the finding holds. In host_documents.js, settleKey (84-94) awaits flushEditor (87). It then hashes ed.getValue() (89) and stores that hash as docFile.key whenever the key is null or `clean` is set (91). Nothing checks whether the document changed during the await.

The path runs in both cases the finding names:
- **Opening a file:** openDocument activates the tab at 286, before `await this.settleKey(ed)` at 288. The file's key starts as null (fileMeta `key: null`, 281), so line 91 always adopts the new hash.
- **Restoring a session:** host_setup.js:248 calls settleKey for each restored tab without awaiting it, after `_restoring--`. The tab is live at that point. A tab saved clean carries `clean`, and line 91 overwrites the file's key.

The wait is real at the sizes the app is tuned for. setValue clears selectionEncoded (inpaint_ed_persist.js 306-307). Above SYNC_ENCODE_PX (16 MP, inpaint_consts.js:109), getValue only starts encodeSelectionSoon (canvasToBlob of the selection's box up to 64 MP, or encodeTilePixels through the pool). flushEditor's selection loop (37-45) waits up to 60 s for that encode.

Two kinds of edit get adopted during that wait:
- **Edits that change no pixels:** moving a layer, changing its opacity or blend, typing a prompt, changing a filter value. getValue includes these straight away, so the hash takes them in.
- **A pixel stroke:** only when the autosave's syncLayers uploads the layer before line 89 runs. Otherwise the layer is still dirty and documentDirty stays true until the stroke is uploaded. After that, bundle() (host_queue.js 526) sets _stateKey to a new hash that differs from the key, so the tab does show dirty.

changed() sets _stateKey to null, but settleKey sets it again at line 90 to the hash it has just adopted. documentDirty (69-77) then compares two equal keys, and the tab shows no '*'. According to the finding, shell.js closeDocument only asks to save when the tab is dirty; I did not open shell.js. A Ctrl+W then closes the tab, and the .scumble on disk never gets the edit.

I rate it should, not must: it needs a large document with a saved selection and an edit in the first seconds. The state is not gone either, because Reopen Closed Tab brings it back.

This is not a repeat of an open item. There is no entry for settleKey, the key or the clean tab in docs/BUGS.md, and none in either verified.json.

The fix direction is right: take a change mark before the await (historyGen or the undo stack, or a counter that changed() raises) and adopt the key only when nothing moved. Otherwise keep the file's key, or leave it null, and drop `clean`.

findings.claim: queueGenerate reads `r = this.recipe` once at its start, but it reads the Settings rows (editor.settings by index) and runs the missing-file check only after several awaits: the LoRA list, boxPromptSlot, the uploads in serializeForPrompt and ensureOnServer. If the user (or an agent's select_recipe) switches recipe during those awaits, the old recipe's graph gets the new recipe's row values by index. missingFilesRefusal then returns nothing because `r !== this.recipe`, and the PNG workflow names the wrong recipe.
findings.scenario: 15k document, 'Flux.2 Klein local' selected. The user clicks Generate, and the base composite and mask take a few seconds to upload. Meanwhile the user picks 'Qwen Image Edit 2.1 local' in the recipe select, to prepare the next run. setRecipe -> applyRecipe -> settingsChanged re-keys editor.settings[0..n] to Qwen's targets with Qwen's file values. queueGenerate resumes with r = Klein. Lines 214-218 write settings[index].value into Klein's prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]. Both recipes load from nodes 'unet', 'clip' and 'vae', so Klein's graph is queued with Qwen's UNet, text encoder and VAE: the sampler fails with 'mat1 and mat2' or renders garbage on the user's ComfyUI. The file check that would catch a missing file is skipped (missingSettingFiles answers [] when r is not the selected recipe), and extra_pnginfo records Qwen as the recipe. A switch to a provider recipe writes values such as 'high' into Klein's loader inputs, and ComfyUI refuses the prompt.
findings.evidence: host_queue.js:30 `const r = this.recipe`. Awaits follow at 83 (loraPlan -> refreshLoraNames fetch), 108/154 (boxPromptSlot fetch), 135/138 (editor.serializeForPrompt uploads) and 189 (ensureOnServer). 211 calls this.missingFilesRefusal(editor, r) -> host_presets.js:525, which returns [] when `r !== this.recipe`. 214-218 write `editor.settings[String(s.index)].value` into `prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]` with no check of entry.target. 263 calls workflowInfo, which reads this.recipe (host_queue.js:396). shell_settings.js:105 selectRecipe -> host.setRecipe (host_setup.js:257) -> applyRecipe (host_presets.js:631) -> ed.settingsChanged (inpaint_canvas.js:983-986) replaces every entry whose target changed, with no guard for a run being queued. runProvider avoids this by reading params at the click (host_provider.js:321). findings.fix: Before the first await in queueGenerate, snapshot the rows for r: for each s of r.settings, take editor.settings[s.index].value only when entry.target === `${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}`. Run missingFilesRefusal against that snapshot then, and use the snapshot at 214-218. Pass r to workflowInfo instead of reading this.recipe. Optionally refuse the queue (or say so) when this.recipe !== r after the uploads.
findings.why: I read host_queue.js queueGenerate. It takes `const r = this.recipe` at line 30. Before line 211 it awaits loraPlan (about 83), boxPromptSlot (108/154), editor.serializeForPrompt (135/138) and ensureOnServer (189). Only an Each-area run checks the recipe again (lines 25, AREA_RECIPE_CHANGED); a plain Generate has no such check. Nothing stops a recipe switch during those waits. The select's change handler (shell.js:464) and the `select_recipe` command (commands_docs.js:138) both call selectRecipe -> host.setRecipe (host_setup.js:257), with no check for a run in progress. setRecipe -> applyRecipe -> ed.settingsChanged (inpaint_canvas.js ~983) replaces every editor.settings[index] entry whose target changed, and it does so for every editor. When queueGenerate resumes, missingFilesRefusal -> missingSettingFiles (host_presets.js:525) returns [] at once because `r !== this.recipe`, so the file check is skipped. Lines 214-218 then write `editor.settings[String(s.index)].value` into `prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]` for r's rows with no check of entry.target. The recipe files confirm the reviewer's example: flux2_klein_local, flux3_klein_local and qwen_image_edit_2_1(_turbo)_local all put rows 1-3 on the nodes unet/clip/vae (unet_name/clip_name/vae_name). A Klein graph would therefore go out with Qwen's model files, and later rows (4 steps, 5 cfg, 6 megapixels/resolution) would mix as well. workflowInfo (line 396) reads this.recipe, not r, so the PNG metadata names the new recipe. This is not host/H-2 in review_full_2026-11-07: H-2 is triggered by a document open or reopen and comes from restore(). This is a recipe switch during the run's own waits. I found no entry for it in BUGS.md. Severity is should: the wrong graph runs or fails on the user's own ComfyUI. Nothing is paid, since provider recipes leave earlier through runProvider, and nothing in the document is overwritten. The fix direction is right: take the rows for r (checking entry.target) before the first await, check files against that copy, and pass r to workflowInfo.

findings.claim: Split into layers refuses any source over 36 MP (6000 x 6000 in area), and nothing in the app scales the source down first. A 15k document (150 MP), or even a 24 MP photo at 6000 x 4000, cannot be split at all. The model answers at about 2K anyway, and planLanding already scales its boxes from the answer's size to the source rect, so a downscaled send would land the same layers.
findings.scenario: A 15000 x 10000 document. Image > Split into Layers (or MCP split_layers) answers 'The picture is 15000 × 10000 (150.00 megapixels): Seedream 5.5 splits pictures of 512 × 512 to 6000 × 6000 in area, no steeper than 16:1.' The same happens for a large layer as source. The only way out is to resize the whole document down, which loses the resolution the user works at, although the layers come back at 2K and are scaled up to the source either way.
findings.evidence: splitlayers.js:176-180 sets rect to the full document (or layer) size and calls splitSizeRefusal(rect.w, rect.h) (36-40, MAX_PIXELS 6000*6000) with no scale step. sourceBytes (198-214) sends flattenToCanvas or the layer at full rect size. planLanding (115-131) maps the answer's boxes with sx = rect.w / bw and sy = rect.h / bh, so it is independent of the size sent. ark.js layerSizeRefusal (443-447) checks the dimensions it receives, so a scaled request would pass. The file header (12-14) expects a larger picture to come back as scaled-up layers.
findings.fix: In sourceBytes, scale the source so it fits the host's area cap (and its minimum edge), for example to at most 6000*6000 px or just above the 2K tier, keeping the aspect ratio. Send that size as width and height, and check splitSizeRefusal against the scaled size instead of rect. Keep rect for planLanding, and refuse only a source too small or too steep.
findings.why:
I checked this in the code and it holds. One example in the claim is wrong.

What I read in splitlayers.js:
- splitJob (lines 176-180) sets rect to the whole document, or to the layer's own size. It then calls splitSizeRefusal(rect.w, rect.h) directly. That check (lines 36-40) uses MAX_PIXELS = 6000*6000, and there is no step that scales the picture down first.
- sourceBytes (lines 198-214) sends either flattenToCanvas or the layer at the full rect size. The run sends width/height = job.rect (line 344).
- The main side repeats the same check on the PNG it receives. ark.js layers() (lines 541-545) runs layerSizeRefusal on the PNG's dimensions, and layersplit.js:45 does the same for WaveSpeed and Oxen. So both sides refuse.
- planLanding (lines 115-131) maps each box with sx = rect.w / bw. The layers are therefore placed the same way whatever size was sent, and readyRow already scales every answer to its row. Scaling the source to fit 36 MP before sending, while keeping rect for the landing, would give the same layers.
- The header (lines 11-13) says the answer is "at most about 2K", so pixels above 36 MP add nothing.

Correction: the 6000 x 4000 example is wrong. That picture is 24 MP, which is under 36 MP at a 1.5:1 ratio, so it passes. The real refusal starts above 36 MP. The 15000 x 10000 case (150 MP) is refused as the claim says, and so is any layer above 36 MP.

Not a repeat: BUGS.md's only split entry is about a run lost on reload, and neither verified.json mentions splitSizeRefusal or splitJob.

Why it is not refuted: MANUAL.md:562 documents the refusal ("Scumble refuses anything else before it sends"), so the limit is deliberate. Still, it shuts the feature off completely on the 15k documents the app is tuned for, with no technical reason. Other features already scale the input down instead of refusing it (the Key box in MANUAL.md:519, the Realism Pass at 423, FLUX 3 references).

Fix direction: scale the source to fit the area cap, while keeping the minimum edge and the 16:1 ratio. Check the refusal against the scaled size, and keep rect for planLanding. A scaled send also keeps the PNG under the 30 MB input limit (RECIPES.md:2904).

findings.claim: readIndex swallows every error, including EBUSY/EPERM and a damaged brushes.json, and returns []. list() therefore never throws, so the renderer's guard (host_generate.js:165 sets brushTipsUnread only when list() rejects) never trips. The next save() then unlinks every stored tip PNG that is not in the now-empty library. brushes.json is also written in place with fsp.writeFile (truncate, then write), so a crash or power loss mid-write leaves exactly the damaged index that sets this off.
findings.scenario: The user has 40 imported .abr tips. brushes.json is truncated by a crash during an earlier tip save, or is held by an antivirus or backup scan at start. At start list() returns [], and the library comes up empty with no warning. The user imports one new tip, and saveBrushTips sends [newTip]. save() keeps only that id and runs fsp.unlink on the other 40 <id>.png files (brushes.js:54-57), then writes an index of one entry. Every imported tip is gone for good.
findings.evidence: brushes.js:17-24 readIndex: try { JSON.parse(readFile) } catch (_) { return [] }. brushes.js:27-37 list() only awaits readIndex, so it cannot reject on a read or parse failure. brushes.js:43-59 save(): keep = the ids sent; the readdir loop at 54-57 unlinks every other /^[a-z0-9]+\.png$/; the index is written at 58 with a plain fsp.writeFile, which is not atomic. Renderer: host_generate.js:165 sets brushTipsUnread only in the catch of brushes.list(), and host_generate.js:202 skips the save only when it is set. That guard is dead code for these failures. settings/keys/autosave got the 'only ENOENT means empty, damaged goes aside' treatment in fix-main pack 1 (D3/MAIN-7); brushes.js did not.
findings.fix: In readIndex, return [] only on ENOENT. Rethrow a read error, and move a damaged index aside (as settings.js setAsideDamaged does) and throw, so list() rejects and the renderer's brushTipsUnread guard works. Write brushes.json through a temp file + fsync + rename. Optionally, in save(), refuse to delete PNGs when the index on disk could not be read in this process.
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. brushes.js:17-24 readIndex catches every error, not only ENOENT, and returns []. That covers a parse error on a truncated brushes.json and EBUSY/EPERM on the read. list() (27-37) only awaits readIndex, so it cannot reject for these. main.js:1296 passes brushes.list() straight to ipcMain.handle with no wrapper. As a result the renderer's guard never fires: host_generate.js:165 sets brushTipsUnread only in the catch of brushes.list(), and saveBrushTips (202) skips the save only when that flag is set. The library loads empty with no warning. The next saveBrushTips, which runs on any tip import or change through editor.onBrushTips, sends only the tips in the library. save() (43-59) builds keep from those ids, and the readdir loop at 54-57 unlinks every other <id>.png. The index is written at 58 with a plain fsp.writeFile: it truncates first and is not atomic, so a crash mid-write leaves exactly the damaged JSON that sets this off. A second way in, same root cause: list() line 34 also drops an entry when its PNG read fails for any reason, a transient EBUSY included, and the next save then deletes that PNG. Neither BUGS.md nor either verified.json mentions brushes.js or readIndex. The fix direction is right: only ENOENT should mean empty; any other failure should set a damaged index aside or rethrow so list() rejects; write through temp + rename. Severity: should, not must. The user loses imported tips for good, but it needs a damaged or locked index, and the tips can usually be imported again from their .abr files.

findings.claim: While settings.json cannot be read (the transient EBUSY/EPERM case the fix-main pack 1 change was made for), get() hands out DEFAULTS as if they were the user's settings, and set() collects patches in `pending`. Callers compute those patches from the default copy: whole maps such as recipeValues, recipeLoras, recipePresets, recipeProviders, nodeParams, pluginData, plugins and recentDocuments, rewritten from what get() returned. When a later read succeeds, get() writes {...DEFAULTS, ...stored, ...pending}. The pending top-level keys replace the stored ones, so the user's stored maps are replaced by the near-empty ones built during the outage.
findings.scenario: At start, settings.json is held for a moment by an antivirus, backup or sync tool, and the read fails after the 4 retries. shell.js:1371-1374 then sets host.recipeValues/loras/presets to {} and selectRecipe(default) writes {recipe, recipeByMode} (shell_settings.js:131). The user changes one Settings row, and host_presets.js:55 sends {recipeValues: {thatRecipe: ...}}. Main's addRecent sends recentDocuments: [oneFile], and plugins.setData sends pluginData: {id: patch}. Two seconds later any get() (curlfetch calls it on every request) reads the file fine, and line 179 builds cache = {...DEFAULTS, ...stored, ...pending}; lines 184-185 write it. The stored recipeValues for every other recipe, the LoRA rows, the presets, the provider picks, the recent list, the selected recipe and every plugin's data are replaced by the session's one-entry versions. The renderer's own copies stay default-derived for the session, so later writes keep clobbering after the recovery too.
findings.evidence: settings.js:97-129 readJson returns {ok:false, data:{}} on a read error. settings.js:162-189 get(): while !loaded, cache = {...DEFAULTS, ...stored, ...pending} (179) is returned as real; once ok, pending is merged over stored and written (181-185). settings.js:191-199 set(): base = get() (the default-derived cache), pending = {...pending, ...patch}. Whole-map writers: host_presets.js:55, 129, 139; host_queue.js:466; shell_settings.js:102, 131; plugins.js:113-118 setData (pluginData) and 87-95 setEnabled; main.js:941-956 addRecent/dropRecent (recentDocuments). shell.js:1371-1374 seeds host.recipeValues/loras/presets from the settings read at start.
findings.fix: Do not take writes while the store is unread. Make set() throw (callers already catch 'not saved'), or keep pending but merge it per key only where the stored value is still the default at load. Also make settings:get report that the settings are unread, so the window does not seed its in-memory maps from defaults and write them back later.
findings.why:
I read the code at ce4415ec and the defect is there. settings.js readJson (97-113) returns {ok:false, data:{}} when the read fails after its retries with EBUSY, EPERM or EACCES (about 250 ms in all, then a 2 s cooldown). While that lasts, get() (162-189) gives callers cache = {...DEFAULTS, ...stored(={}), ...pending} with loaded=false. Nothing marks it as unread, and the settings:get IPC (main.js:1155) passes it on as is. set() (191-199) adds each patch to `pending`. On the next read that succeeds, line 179 spreads pending over the real stored object and lines 183-185 write the result. That is a shallow, top-level merge, so every key in pending replaces the stored value whole.

The writers do send whole maps built from that default copy:
- At start, shell.js:1371-1373 seeds host.presets, loras and recipeValues with `|| {}`. Those maps are not in DEFAULTS (settings.js:15 says so).
- savePresets and saveLoras (host_presets.js:129, 139) and flushRecipeValues (55) write {...thatMap, [id]: x}.
- selectRecipe (shell_settings.js:131) writes recipe and recipeByMode from the default copy, so the user's chosen recipe is reset too.
- rememberProvider (102) writes recipeProviders the same way.
- Main's addRecent and dropRecent (main.js:941-956) and plugins.setEnabled (plugins.js:87-95) build recentDocuments and plugins from settings.get(), which is the default cache at that moment.

So once the read recovers, the user's stored maps are replaced by the near-empty ones built during the outage. A second problem follows: the window's in-memory maps stay seeded from defaults after the recovery. Every later savePresets, saveLoras or recipeValues write keeps overwriting the stored map, even after loaded=true and even without pending.

Nothing guards against this: no caller checks `loaded`, and get() has no unread flag.

This is not a repeat of review_full_2026-11-07 (verified.json, the fsync / "a transient read error wipes every setting" entry). The pending mechanism was the fix for that entry, and this is a defect left in the fix itself. There is no BUGS.md entry for it.

I rate it should, not must: it loses settings (presets, LoRA rows, per-recipe values, the recent list, plugin data), not pixels or documents. The trigger is also rare: another program has to hold settings.json for more than about 250 ms during a read. That is the same case fix-main pack 1 was built for.

The suggested fix is the right direction. Refuse or defer writes while the store is unread, or merge per key. Also have settings:get report the unread state, so the window does not seed its maps from defaults.

findings.claim: connect() has no generation check. A connect that was started for an earlier URL can finish after a newer connect has already succeeded, and it then overwrites the status. If it fails, the status says "error" and names the new URL while the socket to the new URL stays open. If it succeeds, the status carries the old server's version, node presence, GPUs and OS.
findings.scenario: At start the stored URL is a stopped RunPod pod. connectComfy() at main.js:1513 hangs in `this.json("/system_stats")`: curl's connect-timeout is 30 s for a non-loopback host, undici's is 10 s. Meanwhile the user sets http://127.0.0.1:8188 in Settings › ComfyUI and presses Connect. setUrl disconnects, connect B succeeds, openSocket runs and the status becomes "connected". Then A's fetch rejects. The catch at 220-222 calls setStatus({ state: "error", message: "cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8188: ..." }), because it uses this.url, which is now the new URL. shell.js showStatus passes this to host.setServerStatus. Every readiness check that wants "connected"/"missing-node" then refuses, although the websocket is up: commands_util.js:461 answers 'Not connected to ComfyUI' to MCP agents, and the LoRA panel, keying and the Realism Pass refuse too. This lasts until the user reconnects by hand. In the other order, a slow-but-alive old server finishes last and its os/gpus describe the wrong machine for the Realism Pass check.
findings.evidence: comfy.js:197-224: connect awaits this.json (203) and this.fetch (205). Nothing compares this.url or a counter afterwards. It then sets wsWanted and calls openSocket (211-213) and setStatus (215, 221-222). setUrl (50-57) only disconnects and does not cancel the request in flight. main.js:1044-1058 connectComfy has no serialisation (called from 1170 comfy:connect and 1513 at start). renderer/shell.js:359-371 hands every status to host.setServerStatus. renderer/commands_util.js:461,471 and lora_panel.js:50 gate on st.state.
findings.fix: Take `const gen = ++this.connectGen` at the top of connect(), and after each await return early when `gen !== this.connectGen || this.url !== u` (no setStatus, no openSocket). Also abort the old probe's requests with an AbortController kept on the client.
findings.why:
I read electron/main/comfy.js:197-224 (connect), 50-57 (setUrl), 66-71 (setStatus), 228-257 (disconnect and openSocket), main.js:1044-1058 (connectComfy), 1170 (comfy:connect) and 1513 (the connect at start), and shell.js:359-371 (showStatus). connect() awaits this.json("/system_stats") and this.fetch("/object_info/InpaintCanvas") with no signal, no counter and no check of the URL afterwards. setUrl() changes this.url and calls disconnect(), but it does not abort the request still in flight. connectComfy has no serialisation and nothing cancels the earlier call. curlfetch.js:35 gives a remote host a connect-timeout of 30 s, so the connect at start against a dead remote address can stay pending while the user runs Connect from Settings or the top bar.

When the old call rejects after the new one has succeeded, the catch calls setStatus({state:"error", message:"cannot reach " + this.url ...}). setStatus stamps url: this.url, which is now the new URL. Nothing puts the state back:
- openSocket's "open" handler only patches {socket:true}.
- The "close" handler only patches {socket:false} and reconnects the socket.
- setStatus is only called from connect and disconnect.

So the state stays "error" with a live websocket until the user reconnects by hand. showStatus passes every status to host.setServerStatus, and the readiness gates read st.state (commands_util.js, lora_panel.js), so they refuse.

In the other order the gap is the same: an older, slower call that succeeds last writes its own version, gpus and os, and it also sets wsWanted, which is harmless because this.url is already the new one. Neither BUGS.md nor the two verified.json files cover this race. Their connectComfy entry is about the secret being sent to a new origin.

The fix direction is right. Keep a generation counter taken at entry and return without setStatus or openSocket when it has changed after each await. Optionally abort the old requests with an AbortController that setUrl or disconnect triggers.

Severity is should: the race needs a URL change while a slow connect is still pending, and the user recovers with a manual reconnect. No pixels or money are lost.

findings.claim: The rec-import-overwrite fix is incomplete. importFile now picks ids against the user folder's file stems, lowercased (recipes.js:268, 297, 312), but the ComfyUI window's 'Save as new recipe' still picks an id only against list()'s ids, compared case-sensitively (recipes_graph.js fromGraph 138-141, fromCloudGraph 316-319). save() writes `<id>.json` whenever no recipe has that exact id and never checks whether that file already exists. On Windows' case-insensitive filesystem this overwrites a user recipe whose file name differs from the new id only in case. It also overwrites a user file that failed to parse.
findings.scenario: The user wrote a recipe file by hand as recipes/MyLook.json without an `id` (docs/RECIPES.md describes writing your own). readDir reads its id as "MyLook" (readId keeps upper case). Later, in the ComfyUI window, they save a graph as a new recipe named "MyLook". slug() gives "mylook", and ids (main.js:1094) holds "MyLook" but not "mylook", so the id stays "mylook". save(): `had` finds no recipe with id "mylook", so file = recipes/mylook.json. fsp.writeFile opens and truncates the existing MyLook.json on NTFS, and the user's recipe is gone with no question and no undo. The same happens to a user file that is currently unreadable (readDir skips it, so its stem is in no id list).
findings.evidence: recipes_store.js:672-681: save() looks up `had` by exact id (676), falls back to `id + ".json"` (677) and writes it with fsp.writeFile (680). slug() lowercases (684-686). readId keeps a mixed-case id (85-91). recipes_graph.js:138-141 and 316-319 take `taken = new Set(ids)` and compare case-sensitively. main.js:1094 passes only list ids. Compare recipes.js:237-243 (userFileStems, lowercased) and 312 (fileStems.has(id.toLowerCase())), which only importFile uses.
findings.fix: Make save() refuse to write a new id over an existing file it did not read for that id: when `had` is undefined, check the folder for a name equal to `<id>.json` ignoring case (or open with flag "wx"), and bump or throw. Alternatively pass userFileStems() into fromGraph/fromCloudGraph's `ids` from saveComfyGraph and compare lowercased, as importFile does.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. In recipes_store.js, readDir (around 93-109) sets r.id = readId(r.id || stem). readId keeps upper case, because SAFE_ID allows A-Z. It skips any file that fails to parse, logging only a warning. In main.js, saveComfyGraph (around 1090-1094) builds ids from list() ids only. recipes_graph.js fromGraph (138-141) and fromCloudGraph (316-319) bump the slugged id only against that exact-case Set. save() (672-681) looks up `had` by exact id. When there is none it writes path.join(dir, id + ".json") with a plain fsp.writeFile: no existence check, no "wx" flag, no prompt. The Save as new path never asks the user either.

So "MyLook.json" with no id lists as "MyLook". Save as new named "MyLook" slugs to "mylook", which is not taken, so save() writes mylook.json. On NTFS that opens and truncates MyLook.json. An unreadable user file is overwritten the same way, since it is in no id list.

The defect is wider than case. Any user file whose stem differs from the id inside it is hit, on any filesystem: foo.json holding id "bar" is overwritten by Save as new "foo".

The importFile fix guards only its own path: userFileStems is lowercased, and recipes.js:297 and 312 check it. The Save as new path has no such guard.

It is not known. BUGS.md's recipe entry (around line 132) is about relight ids. verified.json's importFile finding is the one the new fix addressed. The fromGraph Save to recipe finding (around line 634) is about the held-id overwrite, not a new id colliding with a file.

The fix direction is right. In save(), when `had` is undefined, refuse or bump if the folder already holds `<id>.json` under any case: compare a case-insensitive readdir, or write with flag "wx". Or pass userFileStems into saveComfyGraph's ids and compare lowercased. The first also covers every other caller.

Severity should, not must. It loses a user's recipe without warning and with no undo, but only when a recipe file was written by hand or renamed, or is broken.

findings.claim: On Windows, the curl that is used is System32\curl.exe, which uses Schannel, and Schannel's certificate revocation check is strict by default. The config does not set `ssl-revoke-best-effort`. So on a machine where the CRL/OCSP endpoints cannot be reached, every HTTPS request through the switch fails with CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK (0x80092012). Unreachable endpoints are typical behind TLS-inspecting proxies or antivirus HTTPS scanning, the environments this feature exists for. The switch is on by default and never falls back to Node's fetch on a TLS failure.
findings.scenario: A Windows user behind a TLS-inspecting company proxy (or an antivirus with HTTPS scanning) whose inserted root CA is in the Windows store, with revocation endpoints that do not answer. Settings › Network is on by default, so route() sends fal.ai, Replicate, OpenAI, model downloads and so on through curl. Schannel cannot complete the revocation check, and curl exits 35 ('schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: ... 0x80092012'). curlFetch rejects with TypeError 'fetch failed' for every provider run and every helper-model download. The only way out is to find Settings › Network and turn curl off. A browser on the same machine works, because Chromium soft-fails revocation.
findings.evidence: curlfetch.js:44-48 prefers %SystemRoot%\System32\curl.exe (the Schannel build). The config at 96-102 holds silent, show-error, globoff, no-buffer, suppress-connect-headers, connect-timeout and speed-limit, and no ssl-revoke-best-effort / ssl-no-revoke. route() (301-309) falls back to node only when no curl is found. A curl failure becomes failed(stderr) at 160 and is never retried on Node. This depends on Schannel's documented default (curl's --ssl-revoke-best-effort, 7.70+, exists for exactly this case) and was not run here.
findings.fix: On win32, push "ssl-revoke-best-effort" into the config. It is accepted by curl 7.70+, and Windows' bundled curl is 8.x; check probe()'s version, or retry once with it on exit 35 whose stderr names revocation. Say in Settings › Network's status which TLS backend curl uses.
findings.why:
I read electron/main/curlfetch.js at ce4415ec. On win32, candidates() (lines 44-48) puts %SystemRoot%\System32\curl.exe first. On this machine that binary reports "libcurl/8.22.0 Schannel", so the Windows build always runs the Schannel backend. hop()'s config (lines 96-102 onwards) has no ssl-revoke-best-effort or ssl-no-revoke anywhere, and neither the file, BUGS.md, TESTING.md nor the two verified.json files mention revocation or Schannel, so this is not a known entry. route() (lines 300-308) falls back to Node only when the setting is off or probe() finds no curl. A curl exit with an error rejects through failed(stderr) in finish() and is never retried on Node. install() wraps every non-loopback fetch, and the setting is on by default.

curl's Schannel backend checks revocation strictly by default; --ssl-revoke-best-effort (7.70+) exists for exactly this case. The failure is CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK (0x80092012) when the CRL/OCSP endpoint cannot be reached, or when the leaf has no distribution point. That is typical of certificates issued by TLS-inspecting proxies and antivirus HTTPS scanning, the environments this feature was built for. It is also a widely reported failure of Windows curl and git-schannel behind such setups. In that case every provider run, upsampler call and model download fails with "fetch failed" until the user finds Settings › Network.

It is also a regression for a machine whose firewall only blocks CRL hosts: Node's fetch, which does no such check, worked there before curl became the default.

I did not run it live. The verdict rests on the code path, which is certain, and on Schannel's documented default.

Severity: should, not must. It is a wrong-result failure of every request with a settings switch as the way out; nothing is paid, and no pixels or documents are lost.

The fix direction is right: push "ssl-revoke-best-effort" into the config on win32, since the bundled curl is 8.x. Optionally gate it on probe()'s version, or show the TLS backend in the Network status. Line 96 is the right anchor: the config array opens there.

findings.claim: PRV-1's shared poller checks the wall-clock deadline at the top of its loop, before it reads the status again, and it gives up after 5 failed reads in a row (backoff 1+2+3+4+5 s, about 15 s). A paid fal, Replicate or WaveSpeed job is dropped when the machine sleeps past the deadline and the first read after waking fails. It is also dropped when the network is gone for about 15 s. Nothing is noted for recovery, and fal and Replicate even send their stop request.
findings.scenario: A Replicate or fal edit is submitted. The user closes the laptop lid for 20 minutes. The job finishes on the provider in a minute and is billed. On wake, the pending pause resolves and the status GET fails (ENOTFOUND or ECONNRESET while Wi-Fi reconnects), so `continue` runs. The loop top sees elapsed > waitMs (15 min) and throws timedOut ('timed out after 15 minutes ... may still finish and be charged'). replicate.js:253 and fal.js:293 then call askStop on the finished job. The picture stays on the provider and is never fetched. No cloudjobs note is written for these providers, so the window cannot bring it back. Without sleep, a VPN or Wi-Fi drop of about 15-20 s ends the run the same way, and downloadImage's 3 tries (about 4.5 s) loses the finished picture.
findings.evidence: util.js pollJob: lines 242-249 throw on `rem <= 0` before any further read. Lines 255-264 count a thrown fetch as a miss and `continue` straight back to that check. Lines 260/274 give up after POLL_FAILURES_MAX = 5 with nextWait = 1000*misses. downloadImage (190-210) uses RESULT_TRIES = 3 with waits of 1.5 s and 3 s. Callers: fal.js queued 260-298 (askStop on timedOut at 293), replicate.js 214-256 (askStop at 253), wavespeed.js submitAndWait 378-390. Compare comfycloud.js finishV2 (comment 1192-1199): it tolerates STATUS_GAP_MS = 120 s of unanswered reads, reads first after a sleep past the deadline, and keeps a job note.
findings.fix: In pollJob, check the deadline only after an answered status read. Unanswered reads should continue for a time window (about 120 s, measured as in finishV2) rather than a count of 5, even past waitMs. Give each read its own timeout (AbortSignal.any with ~30 s) so a half-open socket after a wake does not block for 300 s. Never askStop on a timeout whose last read was not answered. Give downloadImage the same time-based window.
findings.why: I read util.js pollJob (219-282), pause (124-156), downloadImage (190-210), and the fal.js queued (249-298), replicate.js (219, 250-253) and wavespeed.js (383) callers. The code is as the reviewer says. POLL_FAILURES_MAX = 5 (line 74). A thrown fetch counts a miss, sets nextWait = 1000*misses and `continue`s. The loop then checks `rem <= 0` at the top (243-249) and throws { timedOut: true }, before any further read. So only an answered read that shows done can beat the deadline. In the sleep case, the read after waking does happen, because rem was computed before the pause. But if that one read fails (DNS or a reset while Wi-Fi reconnects), the next loop top throws timedOut. fal.js:293 and replicate.js:253 then send askStop to a job that has already finished. Without a sleep, a run of 6 thrown reads also ends it: the waits are 1+2+3+4+5 s, and an ENOTFOUND fails fast, so a network drop of about 15-20 s is enough. downloadImage gives up after 3 tries, with about 4.5 s of waiting. None of these providers writes a recovery note; only comfycloud has cloudjobs. The finished, billed picture is then lost. This is not a repeat of a known item. review_full verified.json providers/PRV-1 (the drop after a single failed read) is fixed, and this is a gap in the parameters that fix chose. BUGS.md has no entry on it. The fix direction is sound: put a time window like finishV2's STATUS_GAP_MS on unanswered reads, check the deadline only after an answered read, and send no askStop after a timeout whose last read failed. I keep severity at should rather than must. The loss needs a network outage of 15 s or more, or a sleep longer than the 15-minute waitMs, during a paid run. That is a real money loss, but it is not the common path.

findings.claim: The fix in 12e31828 says a failed Generate new keeps its new tab while a run is still going there, so the answer has somewhere to land. The check it uses is `!busy(fresh)`, and shell.js busy() (line 212) never looks at `_localRuns`. A local ComfyUI render that is still queued or running therefore does not count, and the new tab is force-closed under it.
findings.scenario: The user's tab holds work. They open Generate new with a local ComfyUI recipe while the user's ComfyUI queue is busy, or the model takes longer than 15 minutes. genGo opens `fresh` and runs generate_new with timeout 900. The generate command's loop (commands_runs.js 419-432) never sees an idle queue, so after 900 s plus 30 s it throws "no result arrived". In the catch, busy(fresh) is false: there is no providerPending, and _localRuns is not part of busy(). closeDocument(fresh, { force: true, remember: false }) runs, and host.removeEditor puts the prompt id from _localRuns into _closedPrompts (host_state.js 237-238). The job keeps running on the user's ComfyUI and its picture is thrown away when it finishes. The tab is not on Reopen Closed Tab either. The case the comment describes ('the wait timed out on a busy queue') can only come from this local path, because the provider path of generate_new does not use the timeout.
findings.evidence: shell.js 212-214 busy() lists pending, segmentPending, cutoutPending, upsamplePending, objectsPending, _loading, providerPending and _docSaving, but not _localRuns. shell.js 682-687 is the catch of genGo: `if (fresh && host.editors().includes(fresh) && !busy(fresh)) await closeDocument(fresh, { force: true, remember: false })`. closeDocument itself computes `rendering` from _localRuns (285), and installUpdate (shell_updates.js 207) adds `ed._localRuns.size` for the same reason ('busy() leaves out a render on the user's ComfyUI'). commands_runs.js 98 runs generate with a.timeout, and 419-432 throws after the limit while the job is still queued. host_queue.js 295 adds the prompt id to _localRuns. host_state.js 228-240 removeEditor adds those ids to _closedPrompts, so their results are dropped.
findings.fix: Keep the tab when a local render holds it: `if (fresh && host.editors().includes(fresh) && !busy(fresh) && !(fresh._localRuns && fresh._localRuns.size))`. Or use the same `rendering` test closeDocument uses. Add a generate gate step with a stubbed local run that stays in _localRuns after the timeout.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. shell.js 211-213 busy() checks pending, segmentPending, cutoutPending, upsamplePending, objectsPending, _loading, providerPending and _docSaving. It does not check _localRuns. `pending` is the transform's pending state (inpaint_ed_geometry.js 41), not a run. A local Generate records itself only in _localRuns (host_queue.js 295). closeDocument (shell.js 285) computes `rendering` from _localRuns separately, and its comment says why: "busy() leaves it out".

Local generate_new (commands_runs.js 92-98) calls `ed.newCanvas` on `fresh` and then `COMMANDS.generate.run(ed, { timeout: 900 })`. That loop (419-432) leaves early only when the history grows, the status reads as failed, or /queue goes idle. On a busy production queue, or a render longer than 15 minutes, it runs out the limit. It then waits at least 30 s more (until) and throws "no result arrived". Nothing on that path clears _localRuns. host.js 241 clears it only when queue_remaining is 0.

In the genGo catch (shell.js 684), `!busy(fresh)` is therefore true and `closeDocument(fresh, { force: true, remember: false })` runs. host_state.js 237-238 removeEditor puts the _localRuns ids into _closedPrompts, so the finished picture is dropped. cancelRuns covers only the title row's runs, and cancel_run's text says a plain local Generate is never stopped, so the job keeps using the user's GPU for nothing. With remember:false the tab and its runs are not on Reopen Closed Tab either.

The comment above the check names exactly this case ("the wait timed out on a busy queue"). The provider path of generate_new ignores the timeout, so the guard as written can never protect the case it was written for.

Severity is should, not must. The original tab is untouched, no money is spent (it is a local run), and the cost is lost GPU time and a lost result. Neither docs/BUGS.md nor either verified.json mentions genGo, newTabFrom or this guard.

The suggested fix is right: also keep the tab while `fresh._localRuns.size` is non-zero, or reuse closeDocument's `rendering` test.

findings.claim: An "Undo this turn" card is added after every turn:done, and for every replayed turn:done. Its target is whatever snapshot record assistant_turns.js still holds, and nothing checks that the record belongs to the turn that just ended. So a turn that only read, a turn that failed, or each turn of a reopened saved chat gets a working Undo button that rolls back a different, earlier turn.
findings.scenario: Turn A: "add a paint layer called sky" leaves record {turn: A}. Turn B: "what size is the picture?" only reads, so beforeCall never runs and the record stays A. At B's turn:done, undoCard() calls turnState(), gets A's record and adds a second card labelled "this turn · document 1" under B. A click restores document 1 to its state before turn A and drops the sky layer. If the user edited in between, they lose those edits too after "Undo anyway". A second case: Chats › open a saved chat. openChat() empties the list but never calls forgetTurns(). refresh() then replays the saved events, and each saved turn:done calls undoCard(), so every old turn shows a card bound to the current session's last turn in another chat. main's turnUndone then marks the wrong chat as undone.
findings.evidence: assistant.js:568-578: case "turn:done" calls undoCard() unconditionally, and e.turn is never compared. undoCard 636-651 uses only turnState(). assistant_turns.js:58-68: turnState() returns `record` whatever turn it holds. The record is released only in beforeCall (47), on the next turn's first write. replay 858-866 runs onEvent for every saved event, turn:done included. openChat 714-741 never calls forgetTurns(); newChat (805) and resetAssistant (747) do. main index.js:1011 already keeps lastTurn only when steps > 0 && docs.size, but the panel never reads state.lastTurn.
findings.fix: In onEvent's turn:done, call undoCard() only when turnState() exists and its turn === e.turn. Skip undoCard during replay(), or check lastTurn from state. Call forgetTurns() in openChat.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. In renderer/assistant.js:568-578 the `turn:done` case calls undoCard() every time and never looks at e.turn. undoCard (636-651) and askThenUndo (653-675) use only turnState(). In assistant_turns.js, turnState (58-68) returns whatever `record` is held, and the record is replaced only in beforeCall (43-55), when a later turn makes its first write. The panel's `turn:start` handler (528-532) does not clear it either. Reads never reach beforeCall, because main's metaFor (assistant/index.js:127-143) sets `turn: undefined` for READS and shell.js:1324-1328 snapshots only when meta.turn is set. Main itself keeps lastTurn null for a turn that only read (index.js:830, 1011), but the panel never checks that.

So a read-only turn B after a writing turn A gets a second card that says "this turn". Clicking it restores turn A's snapshot. The reverse case is the same defect: once B writes, the old card under A is still live and would undo B, because the target is resolved at click time.

The replay case also holds. openChat (714-741) resets the list but does not call forgetTurns(), unlike resetAssistant (747) and newChat (805). Then refresh() calls replay() (858-866), which runs onEvent for every saved event, `turn:done` included, so every old turn of the opened chat gets a card bound to the record from the previous chat. A click also calls api().turnUndone, which marks the newly opened chat as undone (index.js:538-548).

Severity stays should, not must. The user has to click, the "You edited ... since this turn started" check still asks before discarding the user's own edits, and the restore is pushed as one undo step, so Ctrl+Z takes it back. The proposed fix is right in direction: a card only when turnState().turn === e.turn, none during replay, and forgetTurns() in openChat. Old cards should also re-check the turn id at click time. This is not in BUGS.md or in either verified.json; the only related entry there is restoreTurn's missing turnBlocked check, which is a different defect.

findings.claim: Every colour render builds a new scene. Each time it creates a new shadow-casting DirectionalLight with a 2048 x 2048 shadow map, a new ground PlaneGeometry and a ShadowMaterial, and none of them is disposed. three.js r186 therefore allocates a fresh WebGLRenderTarget plus DepthTexture (about 32 MB of GPU memory) per render. The dialog's preview renders once per animation frame while the user drags or moves a slider.
findings.scenario: The user opens Place 3D object and drags to turn the model for 5 s: about 300 previews. That is about 300 shadow targets of ~32 MB each, roughly 9 GB of GPU allocations, freed only if V8 happens to collect the light objects (GC does not see GPU memory). The plugin context can be lost, and VRAM is squeezed on the GPU process the 15k editor's tile compositor shares. Every Edit / glb_edit adds one more.
findings.evidence: render.js:260-270: `new THREE.DirectionalLight`, `light.castShadow = !!p.shadow` (default true), `light.shadow.mapSize.set(2048, 2048)`. render.js:271-276: new PlaneGeometry and ShadowMaterial per call. render() 288-298 only removes model.inner, and nothing calls light.shadow.dispose(), geometry.dispose() or material.dispose(). vendor/three.module.js:9300-9304: a light whose shadow.map is null gets `new WebGLRenderTarget(...)` and `new DepthTexture(...)`. dialog.js:130-144 and 150-162: draw() calls renderer.render(...) on each rAF after every pointermove or slider input.
findings.fix: Keep one light (with its shadow) and one ground mesh on the GlbRenderer and update their parameters per render. Or, after each render, call light.shadow.dispose(), ground.geometry.dispose() and ground.material.dispose().
findings.why: I read plugins/glb/render.js:240-298. Every call to scene() creates a new THREE.DirectionalLight with castShadow = !!p.shadow (the default is true, line 16) and shadow.mapSize 2048x2048. It also creates a new ground Mesh with a new PlaneGeometry and a ShadowMaterial. render() removes only model.inner afterwards; nothing calls light.shadow.dispose(), geometry.dispose() or material.dispose(). In the vendored three.js r186, WebGLShadowMap allocates when shadow.map === null (three.module.js:9254) and then calls `new WebGLRenderTarget(...)` plus `new DepthTexture(..., UnsignedIntType)` (9300-9304). That is about 16 MB of colour plus 16 MB of depth per new light. I checked the call path in dialog.js:129-143: draw() calls renderer.render(...) once per requestAnimationFrame, and schedule() is called on every pointermove while dragging and on every wheel event. So every preview frame allocates a fresh 2048^2 shadow target, uploads it and clears it. WebGLProperties is a WeakMap (7997), so the GL texture and framebuffer are freed only when the Blink wrappers are garbage-collected. That GC is driven by heap pressure, not by VRAM, so GPU memory piles up while the user drags, on the GPU process the editor's tile compositor shares. There is also a strong leak that never goes away: WebGLGeometries keeps `geometries = {}` keyed by geometry.id (4132) and WebGLBindingStates keeps `bindingStates = {}` (1617). Neither entry is removed without geometry.dispose(), so each ground PlaneGeometry and its VAO and buffers stay alive for good. That leak is small per render, but it grows with every preview frame and every Place / glb_edit. Neither docs/BUGS.md nor the two verified.json files mention this; their only glb item is the openGeneration plugin-data loss, which is a different defect. The fix direction is right: keep one light (with its shadow) and one ground mesh on GlbRenderer and update their parameters per render, or dispose the shadow, geometry and material after each render. I kept severity at should rather than must, because no pixels or documents are lost and the shadow targets do get reclaimed at a major GC.

findings.claim: Placing a 3D object from the panel, the Plugins menu or an external MCP call records no undo step: Document.addLayer pushes none, and the depth layer's set_layer role/visible pushes none either. Editing an object records two to four separate steps instead of one: setPixels, set_layer geometry, and then the same pair for the depth layer.
findings.scenario: (a) The user paints a stroke on another layer, then places a 3D object. One Ctrl+Z reverts the stroke and the 3D layer stays. (b) Edit 3D object moves and enlarges the render. The first Ctrl+Z reverts only the depth layer's set_layer. The next two leave the new, larger render squeezed into the old box until the fourth press. Only the assistant path is covered, because policy.undoStep pushes a "layers" step before glb_place.
findings.evidence: main.js:143-162: existing → doc.setPixels (renderer/plugins.js:146 pushes 'layer'/'layerfull'), then doc.run('set_layer', {x,y,w,h}) (its own transform step), and the same for prevDepth. New → doc.addLayer (plugins.js:162-176 calls editor.addLayer, which records no step: inpaint_ed_layers.js:527 'no undo step'). Then set_layer role/visible: soft fields, no step (policy.js SET_LAYER_SOFT). Plugin commands get no undo wrapper (commands_util register, plugins.js:688-690).
findings.fix: Push one 'layers' step (doc.editor.pushUndo({kind:'layers', label:'3D object'})) at the start of place(). Then call setPixels with {undo:false} and set the geometry without its own step, so one placement or edit is one Ctrl+Z.
findings.why: I read plugins/glb/main.js place() (lines 131-166). For a new object it calls doc.addLayer, and renderer/plugins.js:162-176 forwards that to editor.addLayer, which only bumps historyGen ("no undo step", inpaint_ed_layers.js:528). remember() goes through documents.data().set() without the undo option (plugins.js:711-716), so it pushes no "data" step either. Commands registered by plugins are wrapped without any undo (plugins.js:688-690), commands.run adds none (commands.js:118-125), and the panel button and the two Plugins-menu actions (main.js:218/228/238/239) call placeInteractive -> place directly. Plugin docs and the editor have no other pushUndo on this path. So with the default depth_layer false (main.js:251), placing an object records no step at all. Scenario (a) holds: after a stroke and then a placement, Ctrl+Z takes back the stroke and the 3D layer stays. The reviewer gets one detail wrong. set_layer role does push a step: setLayerRole calls pushUndo({kind:"layers"}) (inpaint_ed_refs.js:259). With depth_layer on, a new placement therefore gets one "Layer role" step, taken after both addLayer calls. Undoing it only resets the depth layer's role and leaves both new layers in place, so the conclusion stands. The edit path is confirmed as several steps. setPixels pushes layer/layerfull (plugins.js:146), set_layer geometry pushes "transform" (commands_layers.js:63), and the same pair follows for the depth layer: four Ctrl+Z presses in all. After the colour layer's transform step is undone and before its layerfull step is, the new render sits squeezed in the old box. The step order is off by one from the reviewer's text, but the defect is the same. Not in BUGS.md or either verified.json (the only glb mention there is the openGeneration plugin-data finding, which is a different defect). The fix direction is right: one "layers" step at the start of place(), setPixels with {undo:false}, and the geometry set without its own transform step (for example directly on the layer, or after the snapshot without set_layer's pushUndo). No pixels or documents are lost, so the severity stays should.

findings.claim: The Responses and Gemini adapters report `input` as the provider's total prompt count, which already includes the cached tokens. models.costOf then prices `input` at the full rate and adds `cacheRead` on top, so cached tokens are counted twice. Gemini's thoughtsTokenCount is also left out of output and never priced. The chat adapter subtracts the cached tokens, which shows the intended convention.
findings.scenario: Turn 10 of a chat on gpt-5.6-terra: input_tokens 100,000, 90,000 of them cached. The cost line shows 100k×$2 + 90k×$0.20 = $0.218 instead of 10k×$2 + 90k×$0.20 = $0.038, about 5.7x too high. The panel also shows "190k tokens in". On Gemini 3.1 Pro with thinking, every thought token is missing from the shown cost: candidatesTokenCount excludes thoughts, as the test fixture's total 100+20+5 = 125 shows. Users decide on the model by these numbers.
findings.evidence: responses.js:145-156: `input: Number(u.input_tokens)`, `cacheRead: input.cached_tokens` with no subtraction. gemini.js:196-206: `input: promptTokenCount`, `cacheRead: cachedContentTokenCount`, `output: candidatesTokenCount`, with reasoning kept apart. models.js:123-124: `amount = input*inRate + output*outRate; amount += cacheRead*cacheRate`, and the comment at 91-93 says reasoning is "part of output". chat.js:194 does `input: prompt - cacheRead - cacheWrite`. assistant.js:614 and index.js:1003 add input + cacheRead.
findings.fix: Responses: input = input_tokens - cached_tokens (floored at 0). Gemini: input = promptTokenCount - cachedContentTokenCount, and output = candidatesTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount.
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. In responses.js:145-156, usageOf sets `input: Number(u.input_tokens)` and `cacheRead: input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and never subtracts one from the other. OpenAI's Responses API counts the cached tokens inside input_tokens, so they are in both fields. gemini.js:196-206 does the same thing with promptTokenCount and cachedContentTokenCount; Google documents promptTokenCount as the full prompt, cached content included. It also sets `output: candidatesTokenCount` and keeps thoughtsTokenCount only under `reasoning`. models.js costOf (around 111-124) prices `input` at the input rate, then adds `cacheRead` at the cache rate, so cached tokens are paid twice. Its doc comment says reasoning tokens "are part of output and are not priced again", so Gemini's thought tokens, which Google bills as output and does not count in candidatesTokenCount, are never priced. The fixture's total of 125 = 100+20+5 in assistant_test.js:421 and assistant_mock.py:712 shows they are separate. chat.js usageOf (around 186-200) does `input: Math.max(0, prompt - cacheRead - cacheWrite)` with the comment "`prompt_tokens` includes the cached tokens on this family", which shows the intended convention: `input` means the uncached part. The token counts are wrong as well. index.js:982 adds the fields into chat.usage, and both index.js:1003 (input + cacheRead) and renderer/assistant.js:614 (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite) count the cached tokens twice. The tests never catch it because their Responses and Gemini fixtures have cached_tokens 0 and no cachedContentTokenCount. I found nothing for usageOf, cached_tokens or costOf in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json, so it is not known. I rate it should, not must: it is a wrong cost and token figure in the assistant panel and log, and real money is not spent because of it. The figure can still steer the user's model choice: on long chats it is several times too high on OpenAI Responses and Gemini, and Gemini's thinking cost is left out. The fix direction is right: subtract the cached count from input (floored at 0) in both adapters, and add thoughtsTokenCount to Gemini's output.

findings.claim: Deleting the open chat while its turn runs does not stop the turn, and the turn's done() saves the chat again, with its screenshots. resetAll waits for turnDone, but done() starts saveChat fire-and-forget, so that write can land after store.removeAll().
findings.scenario: While a turn waits on an ask card or a generate, the user opens Chats and clicks × on the current chat ("Delete this chat and its screenshots"). Files and folder are removed and this.chat is set to null. When the turn ends, done() → saveChat(chat) writes <id>.json and every picture back. Settings › reset everything during a turn can likewise leave the last chat on disk, or a "could not be saved" line in a log that was just cleaned.
findings.evidence: index.js:551-556 deleteChat removes files and sets this.chat = null, with no busy check and no mark on the running turn's chat object. done() at 1016: this.saveChat(chat).catch(...), not awaited. saveChat 559-564 checks only readOnly. resetAll 571-584: stop(), await turnDone (which resolves before the save finishes), then store.removeAll().
findings.fix: Mark the chat as deleted (chat.deleted = true) in deleteChat and resetAll, and have saveChat skip it. In resetAll, also await the pending save (keep its promise) before removeAll.
findings.why:
I read the code and the bug is real. It is not in BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for deleteChat, saveChat and resetAll finds nothing).

Delete path:
- The Chats button (renderer/assistant.js:136/197) and the per-row x button (703-708) are never disabled while busy.
- `_startTurn` saves the chat at the end of every turn, so the current chat is in the list from its second turn on.
- `deleteChat` (index.js:551-556) calls store.remove (store.js:107: rm of <id>.json and the picture folder) and sets this.chat = null and this.events = []. It does not check `this.turn` and does not mark the chat object.
- The running turn keeps its own `chat` reference (index.js:381). When it ends, `done()` (1016) calls `saveChat(chat)` without awaiting it.
