- `saveChat` (559-564) checks only `readOnly`, then store.save (store.js:40-66). That runs mkdir, writes every image stripped from chat.history (the screenshots) and renames the JSON into place.
- Result: the chat the user deleted comes back on disk with its screenshots, and it shows in the list again. Its events are those pushed into the fresh this.events array, and its history is the whole history.

Reset path:
- `resetAll` (571-584) awaits `turnDone`. That promise resolves as soon as `done()` returns, which is before the fire-and-forget save's fs writes have finished.
- `store.removeAll` (rm -rf of the root) can therefore run alongside the save's mkdir and writes, and leave the chat file or folder behind after "every chat ... is gone". This race is narrower but plausible.

The fix direction is right: mark the chat deleted in `deleteChat` and `resetAll` and have `saveChat` skip it, and in `resetAll` keep the pending save's promise and await it before `removeAll`.

Severity: should, not nice. Deleting a chat is the user's privacy action, and it is undone silently with the screenshots. It happens in ordinary use: opening Chats while waiting on a generate or an ask card, which can take tens of seconds.

findings.claim: Extend bakes the visible picture into the new base and keeps only control and reference layers. Hidden layers are not in the flatten (drawLayersInto skips layers that are not shown), so their pixels leave the document entirely. The status line only says the border is selected.
findings.scenario: Two of three result layers are hidden for comparison, and a hidden paint layer holds a rough sketch. Drag the Canvas frame outward and press Enter. The hidden results and the sketch are gone from the layer list and from the picture, with no word. They come back only through Ctrl+Z, and only while that step is within the 30-step / 384 MB history.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_geometry.js 1504: `const flat = this.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })`. inpaint_ed_composite.js 72 skips `!this.shown(layer)`. 1542: `const kept = this.layers.filter((l) => this.isControl(l) || this.isReference(l))` and 1554 `this.layers = kept`. The status at 1576 says nothing about layers. CHANGELOG notes that extend bakes the layers, but a hidden layer is not baked: it is deleted.
findings.fix: Keep hidden layers (shift them by left/top as references are), or at least name the dropped hidden layers in the status line and in the assistant's ask card.
findings.why: I read inpaint_ed_geometry.js 1485-1582. extendCanvasNow flattens with `flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })` (1504), which leaves out layers that are not shown. Line 1542 then keeps only control and reference layers, and 1554 replaces `this.layers` with that list. So a hidden paint or result layer is in neither the new base nor the layer list. Nothing guards against this before the cut. The Canvas tool's Enter path reaches the same code: applyCanvasFrame at 1256 calls `extendCanvas(pos)`. The status at 1576 says only that the border is selected. The data is not lost for good, because the canvas undo step (`snapshot({kind:"canvas"})`, pushed at 1564) holds the old layers, so Ctrl+Z brings them back while that step is still in the history. Hence nice, not must. The baking is on purpose (comment at 1541; the CHANGELOG's assistant section says extend canvas "bakes your layers in"). Dropping hidden layers without a word is the gap. flattenNow (inpaint_ed_composite.js 770) drops hidden layers the same way, but that button says "Flatten all visible layers", while nothing about Extend says it deletes hidden layers. Not known: docs/BUGS.md has no such entry. The one extendCanvasNow finding in review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json (line 321) is the upload race (layers changed during the await), a different defect. Fix direction: keep hidden layers and move them by left/top as the kept layers are moved, or at least name them in the status line.

findings.claim: The compare divider's hit zone is active whenever `this.compare` is non-null, but the divider is drawn and used only when both a and b are set. setCompare leaves a half-set compare ({a, b: null}) when there is no other result layer. From then on, every press within 6 device px of the canvas's horizontal middle becomes an invisible 'split' drag.
findings.scenario: With one result layer, Ctrl+click its history thumbnail (status: "A set; choose the other result too."). Brush strokes, selections and clicks that start on the vertical centre line of the view do nothing until compare is ended, and nothing on screen shows why.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_pointer.js 351: `if (this.compare && Math.abs(cx - this.canvas.width * (this.compare.split ?? 0.5)) <= 6 * dpr) { this.pointer = { kind: "split" }; return; }`. inpaint_ed_view.js setCompare 763-770 can leave b null. drawOverlays 701 draws the divider only `if (this.compare && this.compare.a && this.compare.b)`.
findings.fix: Test `this.compare && this.compare.a && this.compare.b` in onPointerDown, as drawOverlays does.
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. inpaint_ed_pointer.js:351 starts a "split" drag for any press within 6*dpr canvas px of canvas.width*split whenever `this.compare` is truthy, and then returns before the tool code runs. inpaint_ed_view.js setCompare (763-774) can leave a half-set compare: it builds `{a:null,b:null,split:0.5}`, sets one side from h.layerId, and fills the other side only if there is another result layer (767-769). With a single result layer, b stays null. The trigger is real: inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:33 calls setCompare on a Ctrl/Shift+click of a history thumbnail, with no check that a second result exists. toggleCompare refuses with fewer than 2 results, but setCompare does not. Everything else that uses compare checks both sides: drawOverlays at view.js:701, relight.js:661 and geometry.js:259 all test `compare && compare.a && compare.b`. So no divider is drawn, yet presses on the vertical centre line are eaten as split drags; pointer.js:882 then only changes compare.split. Two things soften it: the status line says "A set; choose the other result too.", and Esc ends compare (inpaint_canvas.js:311). The defect is small and only pixels on one line are dead, which makes it "nice". It is not in docs/BUGS.md and not in either verified.json (no matches for setCompare, compare.split or divider). The suggested fix is right: test `this.compare && this.compare.a && this.compare.b` at line 351, as drawOverlays does.

findings.claim: onPointerDown overwrites `this.pointer` for any new pointer while a gesture is under way. Only a healing gesture and a liquify gesture are checked. Moves and ups are not filtered by pointerId either, so a second touch or pen contact discards the stroke in progress. Its stroke buffer is never committed and no undo step is pushed.
findings.scenario: On a touch-screen laptop, paint a long stroke with the mouse or pen while a finger or palm touches the screen. The touch's pointerdown starts a new layerpaint gesture: the first stroke vanishes from the screen and is never written, and both pointers' moves then drive the new one. A smudge in progress loses its release, so markLayerChanged and the release of p.orig / p.src are skipped.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_pointer.js 323-324 handle only `this.pointer.healing` and `kind === "liquify"`. Every later branch assigns `this.pointer = {...}` (for example 562 and 463). onPointerMove (735) and onPointerUp (960) never compare e.pointerId with the gesture's.
findings.fix: Store the pointerId on the gesture. Ignore pointerdown while a gesture is held (or end the old one properly first), and ignore move/up events from other pointers.
findings.why: I read the pointer code and the claim holds. In renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js 457-460, pointerdown, move, up and cancel are bound straight to the handlers with no filter on pointerId or isPrimary. inpaint_style.js:82 gives `.ipc-view canvas` `touch-action:none`, so a touch sends the full pointer sequence instead of a browser pan. onPointerDown (inpaint_ed_pointer.js 319-324) guards only two cases: it refuses while `this.pointer.healing` and it drops a liquify gesture. Every other branch overwrites `this.pointer`, for example smudge at 463 and layerpaint at 493/518/532/562. onPointerMove (735ff) and onPointerUp (960ff) never compare `e.pointerId`. The only per-pointer calls are set/releasePointerCapture. So a second contact during a layerpaint stroke throws the first stroke's buffer away without finishStroke or commitStroke. The second contact's up or cancel then ends whichever gesture is current. A smudge, blur or tone stroke is worse. It already pushed its undo step (453) and writes into layer.px, so its pixels land, but they skip markLayerChanged and the release of p.orig and p.src (1077-1082). That leaves stale match statistics and a clone that lives until GC. No data is corrupted beyond the lost stroke. This is not in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for pointerId and multi-touch found nothing). I keep severity nice: it needs a touch screen and a second contact during a stroke, and Windows palm rejection usually suppresses touch while a pen is near. The fix direction is right: store the gesture's pointerId, ignore downs while a gesture is held (or end the old one properly), and ignore moves and ups from other pointers.

findings.claim: Grow, shrink and feather take their input (a clone or a bitmap of the box) and await the pool or worker. They then write the answer's tiles into whatever this.sel is at that moment, and set the cached bounds from the old selection. Nothing checks that the selection is still the one they read. trackEdit only makes an undo wait; a marquee, a deselect or an MCP-free click do not.
findings.scenario: At 15k, Select › Feather 60 px, then drag a new marquee (or press Ctrl+D) while the job runs, about 0.5 s on tiles (PLAN_WASM_BUILD table: feather 524 ms). The answer writes the feathered old selection over every tile of its box, clearing the empty ones (990, 993): the new marquee is erased inside that box and the old feathered shape reappears. markSelectionChanged(done.bounds) then caches the old shape's bounds as exact. The undo list holds 'Feather' and then 'Rectangle selection', which do not describe what is on screen.
findings.evidence: 985 snap = this.sel.clone(); 987 await editorPool().run('selection', ...); 988-994 this.sel.clear(...) / this.sel.writeRect(...) on the current this.sel; 951-958 the canvas route the same (clearRect + drawImage into the box); featherSelectionNow 1135-1150 and growSelectionNow 1395-1403 push the undo step before the await and markSelectionChanged(done.bounds) after it; trackEdit (inpaint_ed_history.js 957-963) is consulted only by historyStepNow and turns.
findings.fix: Record this.selectionSeq (and the sel object) before the await. If either changed, drop the answer, take the operation's undo entry back, and set a status line (as cancelRange does for a range selection). Or refuse selection edits while one is pending.
findings.why: I read inpaint_ed_select.js. selectionOverTiles (978-1003) clones this.sel and awaits editorPool().run. After the await, its loop at 988-994 calls this.sel.clear / writeRect on whatever this.sel is then, with nothing comparing selectionSeq or the sel object. selectionInWorker (939-968) does the same thing after awaiting createImageBitmap and workerCall: a drawInto with clearRect + drawImage over the box. featherSelectionNow (1132-1150) and growSelectionNow (1391-1405) push their undo step before the await and call markSelectionChanged(done.bounds) after it, which stores the old shape's bounds as exact (cachedBounds, selectionDirty=false). trackEdit (inpaint_ed_history.js 957-963) only puts the promise in _pendingEdits, and only historyStepNow waits on that. Nothing blocks input in the meantime. Pointer-down is held only for pointer.healing (inpaint_ed_pointer.js 323), and the keydown guard in inpaint_canvas.js 333 is also heal-only. Ctrl+D (pointer.js 203) and a deselect click (1010/1016) go to clearSelection (select.js 1428), which clears this.sel in place without waiting. The marquee also writes this.sel in place. The Feather / Grow / Shrink buttons in inpaint_modal.js 596-611 are not modal, so the user can do either while the job runs. The scenario holds: the late answer writes the feathered old shape back over every tile of its box, wipes the new marquee there, and leaves a wrong cached bounds and an undo list that does not match the screen. I checked BUGS.md and both verified.json files and none of them lists this. Fix direction is right: take selectionSeq and the sel object before the await and drop the answer if either changed. I judge it nice, not should. It costs only the selection, not pixels or documents; it can be repaired by hand; and you have to act inside a window of about 0.5 s that only exists at large sizes. MCP commands await featherSelection, so a single agent cannot race it.

findings.claim: After the resample's await, the guard looks the target up by id and compares px. An undo of a 'layers' step makes copies that share px, so the guard passes. The code then pushes the undo step for the live copy but writes the mask onto the stale `target` object.
findings.scenario: Paste mask from a layer of another size (the transformedAsync path, a large mask at 15k), and undo a layer rename or reorder while it resamples. curTarget is the new object with the same px, so the check at 277 passes. pushUndo snapshots curTarget and clears the redo stack. target.maskPx = m goes to the detached object: no mask appears, and the status says 'mask copied'.
findings.evidence: 272 await sm.transformedAsync(...); 276-277 curTarget = this.layers.find(id); if (!curTarget || curTarget.px !== target.px) ... (copies from applySnapshot 574 '{ ...l }' keep the same px); 282 pushUndo({ kind: 'mask', id: target.id }) -> snapshot of curTarget; 283-286 target.maskPx = m; markMaskChanged(target).
findings.fix: Write to curTarget (and compare the object, or a pixels version, rather than px alone).
findings.why:
I read the code and the path runs as claimed. In inpaint_ed_masks.js, maskFromLayer awaits sm.transformedAsync at line 272 when the two layers differ in size or place. After the await, the only checks are the op token (275) and `curTarget.px !== target.px` (276-277). The history code shows that check passes for a new object holding the same pixels:
- snapshotOf builds a 'layers' step from snapshotLayer(l), which is `{ ...l }` (inpaint_ed_history.js 174-175, 367), so px is shared.
- applySnapshot for kind 'layers' replaces this.layers with fresh spreads `{ ...l, ... }` (574), so the restored records again carry the same px.

Nothing stops an undo from running during the wait. historyStepNow waits only for _pendingEdits (992), and maskFromLayer is not registered through trackEdit (the menu's Paste mask calls maskOp directly, masks.js 357). The token at 275 only changes with another mask op.

So: paste a mask between layers of different size on a large document, then press Ctrl+Z on an earlier rename or reorder (a 'layers' step) before the resample ends. curTarget is then a new object with the same px and the guard passes. pushUndo({kind:'mask', id}) snapshots the live layer by id (history 394-396) and clears the redo stack, which loses the redo of the undone step. Lines 283-286 then write maskPx, maskOff and maskEdit, and call markMaskChanged, on the detached `target`. The live layer gets no mask, the status says 'mask copied', and the undo step does nothing.

No pixels or documents are lost: the user sees no mask and can paste again. That is why I rate it nice, not should. The fix is right: write to curTarget, and compare object identity (curTarget !== target) or a pixel version rather than px alone. It is not in BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for maskFromLayer / from_layer finds nothing).

findings.claim: Apply mask refuses only filter layers. On a text layer it bakes the mask into px and drops maskPx, but the layer stays kind 'text'. The next text edit re-renders px from the description, so the parts the mask hid come back and the mask is gone, with no word.
findings.scenario: Text layer 'SALE' with a mask hiding its left half, then mask menu › Apply (or set_mask op apply). Later change the font size: renderTextLayer replaces layer.px with a fresh render. The whole word shows again and there is no mask left to switch on.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_masks.js 309-314 only `layer.kind === 'filter'` is refused; 487-501 layer.px = fromCanvas(masked), maskPx = null; inpaint_ed_text.js 101-129 renderTextLayer (kind 'text') sets layer.px = px from renderText(layer.text).
findings.fix: Refuse 'apply' on text layers (the mask stays live, as patchRefusal does for other pixel writes), or convert the layer to an image layer when the mask is applied.
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. maskOp 'apply' (inpaint_ed_masks.js 309-314) refuses only filter layers. The mask row's Apply button (inpaint_ed_layers.js 1024-1025) is greyed out only for filter layers (isFx). set_mask's 'apply' (commands_layers.js 327) checks only that the layer has a mask. Nothing in inpaint_ed_masks.js stops a text layer from getting a mask: maskFromSelection and the others check only maskBlocked. applyMask (487-503) sets layer.px = fromCanvas(masked) and maskPx = null, but it leaves layer.kind 'text' and layer.text in place. renderTextLayer (inpaint_ed_text.js 101-129) runs for any layer with kind 'text' and a description. It sets layer.px to a fresh render of layer.text, so the next font or size edit brings back the parts the mask hid, and the mask is gone. The rest of the editor turns a text layer into pixels before it bakes into them, which shows the intended behaviour: applyPending (inpaint_ed_geometry.js 162-169) sets kind = 'paint', deletes text and bumps _textToken before its applyMask; merge-down does the same (inpaint_ed_layers.js 484); patchRefusal refuses text layers. Apply mask is the one bake that skips this step. The fix direction is right: refuse it, or convert the layer to paint the way applyPending does, with a 'layers' undo step and the _textToken bump. Severity stays nice. Ctrl+Z through the edit and the Apply step brings the mask back, so no work is lost for good. It is a silent wrong result in an uncommon order of steps. It is not in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json: their only applyMask mention is about applyPending's size check.

findings.claim: frequencySeparation computes its box from the selection and the picture size, then awaits readBoxBytes. That call first awaits relightIdle (relight's full shadow marches), then the pool's stack jobs. After the await it adds the two layers at the old box with no check that the document is still the same picture and size. The depth-map paths use a geometryToken for exactly this.
findings.scenario: With a relight layer on a 15k picture (its full march takes 0.6-1 s per light), the user starts Image > Frequency separation on a face. During the wait an undo of an earlier crop, a turn, or an agent's load_image into the tab runs. The 'Low frequency' / 'High frequency' layers then land at the stale coordinates, offset from the content they were cut from, or on a different picture, as a linear-light pair that visibly corrupts the composite until it is undone.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_filters.js:173-177 box from getBounds / this.width. :181 `await this.readBoxBytes(box, { forRun: true })`, and inpaint_ed_stack.js:751 `await this.relightIdle()`, :754/:759 await holdStack / fillBoxFromStack. :189-199 pushUndo and addLayer at box[0], box[1] with no re-check. Compare inpaint_ed_depth.js:209/566 geometryToken.
findings.fix: Take `const token = this.geometryToken()` (and the base / document identity) before the await. After it, refuse with a status line when the token or `this.base` changed, before pushUndo.
findings.why:
I read inpaint_ed_filters.js:171-205. `box` is computed at 173-177 from getBounds() and this.width/height. Line 181 then does `await this.readBoxBytes(box, { forRun: true })`. readBoxBytes (inpaint_ed_stack.js:747-775) first awaits relightIdle() (751), then holdStack/fillBoxFromStack (754/759). Up to 16 MP that is a few hundred ms of pool work even with no relight layer, and longer while relight's full march is pending. After the await, 189-197 call pushUndo and addLayer at box[0]/box[1] without checking geometrySeq, width/height or base.

Nothing stops another edit during the wait. shell.js:1206-1215 only awaits the call; commands_layers.js:84 is the same with no busy lock; inpaint_ed_history.js has no busy guard. So a keyboard undo of a crop or turn, or an agent's load_image / rotate_canvas, can run in between. The pattern used elsewhere for this case confirms the gap: eacharea.js:483/501 and splitlayers.js:336/375 compare geometrySeq (plus w/h) after their awaits, and the depth paths use geometryToken().

The fix direction is right: take geometrySeq, width, height and base before the await, and refuse with a status line before pushUndo when any changed. Comparing geometrySeq alone may not catch an undo that restores the size, so the size check matters too.

Impact: the two layers land offset or on a different picture. That is one undo step, which removes them, and the user's pixels below are not touched. It takes a deliberate edit inside a sub-second window. So it is a small edge-case defect, nice rather than should. It is not in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for freq/frequencySeparation/readBoxBytes found nothing).

findings.claim: A key of a layer source with Screen on Auto picks its fill colour in two separate steps. First keyRead fills the layer's transparent parts with a colour guessed from the border ring with no hint, and falls back to green when the guess is null. Then keyScreenColour guesses the screen again, this time excluding the hint. When the two guesses differ, the picture goes out filled green but keyed as blue. The transparent parts of the layer then come back opaque green in the Key layer.
findings.scenario: The source is a pasted blue-screen layer. Screen is Auto and a selection is the hint. The subject reaches the box's border ring, for example because the box is clamped at the picture edge. With the subject counted, the ring mean has no clear lead, so screenFromRing returns null and keyRead fills green (308-309). keyScreenColour (518 in-app, 993 Route B) leaves out hint >= 128 pixels, the ring mean is clearly blue, and the run is sent with screen "blue". CorridorKey keeps the green fill as foreground. Every transparent area of the source layer inside the matte's box lands as opaque green. The refine reads the same green fill (keyBandReader spec.fill), so it does not fix it.
findings.evidence: host_key.js:308 `let fill = ... keying.screenFromRing(raw, cw, ch, [0, 0, cw, ch], null, a).screen;` uses no hint. 309 `if (!fill) fill = "green";`. 476-480 keyScreenColour calls `keying.screenFromRing(prep.image, ..., hint, prep.weight)` with the hint. keying.js:237-262 screenFromRing skips pixels with `hint[i] >= 128`, so the two calls can disagree. keyComfy 993 sends the second answer as `screen` (keyPrompt), while `r.image` / `r.read.fill` carry the first.
findings.fix: Decide the screen once. In keyScreenColour, when the source is a layer (prep.read.fill set) and Screen is Auto, return prep.read.fill if the hinted guess differs. Alternatively, have keyRead take the hint plane and use the same hinted ring for the fill, and refuse (askScreen) instead of falling back to green when that guess is null.
findings.why:
I read the code and the claim holds. In host_key.js keyRead (306-312), for a layer source with Screen on Auto, the fill comes from `keying.screenFromRing(raw, cw, ch, [0,0,cw,ch], null, a)`, which uses no hint. A null answer becomes "green" (309), and that fill is stored in `image` and in `read.fill` (the refine reads the picture again from read.fill). Afterwards keyScreenColour (408-413) runs a second guess on prep.image with the same alpha weight, the same content ring and the hint plane. keying.js screenFromRing (237-258) skips pixels with `hint[i] >= 128`. Without the hint the two calls would agree (the fill has weight 0 in both). With the hint they can differ, and both runs take the second answer: in-app at 518, Route B keyComfy at 993, which still sends r.image with the first fill. Agreeing guesses are clearly the intent: the doc comment at 280-281 says the layer's screen is told before the fill is chosen.

The case is narrow, though. It needs three things together:
(a) The layer has transparent parts inside the box: the selection's box grows past a smaller pasted layer, or the layer is a cutout.
(b) The selection reaches the 3 % ring. boxPlan grows the selection box by 50 % and to at least 768 px, so this happens only where the box is clamped at the picture's edge.
(c) The subject's share of the ring removes the 24-level lead of the unhinted mean but not of the hinted one.

The opposite disagreement, unhinted blue and hinted null, only refuses with askScreen, which is harmless. When all three hold, the transparent parts go out as opaque green under a blue key and land as green in the Key layer. That is a wrong result the user can see, undo and redo with Screen set to Blue. Nothing is paid for or lost, so the severity is nice, not should. I found no matching entry in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json (grep for screenFromRing / keyScreenColour / keyRead). The suggested fix is sound: decide once, e.g. reuse read.fill for a layer source on Auto, or give keyRead the hint and refuse instead of falling back to green.

findings.claim: saveBrushTips calls are not serialized. Main's brushes.save deletes every PNG not in its own list and then rewrites the index, so two overlapping saves can delete a newly imported tip's file. The renderer then marks every library tip saved, so the lost tip is never written again and is gone at the next start.
findings.scenario: The user imports a large .abr (call 1 encodes its tips one toBlob at a time), then right away imports another brush image or changes a tip's spacing (call 2, whose list also holds the new tip B). Main runs both saves at once. Call 2 writes B.png. Call 1's readdir loop then unlinks B.png, because B is not in call 1's keep set. The last index written may still list B. After a restart, brushes.list cannot load B ('bad tip file'), or B is missing from the index. Meanwhile line 213 set t.saved = true for B, so later saves send png: null for it and never put it back.
findings.evidence: host_generate.js:199-216: no queue or in-flight guard. Line 212 awaits window.scumble.brushes.save(tips), then line 213 marks every tip in this.brushLibrary saved, including tips added after `tips` was built. Callers: inpaint_ed_tips.js:125 (import), 64 (remove) and inpaint_modal.js:180 (spacing change) all go through brushTipsChanged -> onBrushTips -> saveBrushTips. electron/main/brushes.js:43-59 writes the PNGs, then readdir + unlink of every file not in `keep`, then the index; each step is awaited, so two calls interleave.
findings.fix: Serialize the saves in the host: keep a promise chain, and when a save is requested while one runs, run one more after it with the library as it is then. Mark saved only the tips whose png went in that call (the `tips` list), not the whole library.
findings.why:
I read host_generate.js:199-216, brushes.js save, main.js:1297 (a plain ipcMain.handle with no queue), and the callers inpaint_ed_tips.js:64/125 and inpaint_modal.js:180. Nothing guards against overlap and nothing serializes the saves. BUGS.md and both verified.json files have no brush-tip entry.

The defect is real, but the root cause is line 213 more than the unlink. The reviewer's scenario is not the likely path. Call 1's `for...of` runs over the live brushLibrary array, so a tip B imported while call 1 is still encoding gets picked up by call 1 as well. And a second import needs a file dialog, so the user cannot finish one inside the short IPC window.

The realistic path is a remove right after a large .abr import. importBrushFiles makes the first new tip active. If the user removes it while call 1 is still running toBlob on dozens of tips, the splice moves the array, and call 1's iterator skips one tip Ak. Ak is unsaved, so call 1 neither writes it nor keeps it. Call 2 (the remove) starts encoding the unsaved tips alongside call 1.

Call 1 finishes first. Line 213 then sets `t.saved = true` on every library tip, Ak included, even though Ak's PNG was never in call 1's list. If call 2 has not reached Ak yet, it sends `png: null` for Ak, and main writes an index that lists Ak with no file behind it. At the next start brushes.list drops Ak ('the file is gone'). Ak stays marked saved, so it is never written again. The same thing happens to any tip added after call 1 built its list and before call 2 encodes it. The unlink race the reviewer describes can happen too, but it is less likely.

Severity: the rare case loses one imported brush tip after a restart, and the user can re-import it from the .abr. No pixels or documents are lost, so nice. The fix direction is right: chain the saves, and mark saved only the library objects whose PNG went into that call's list.

findings.claim: When settings.json parses badly and setAsideDamaged cannot rename it (EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES), readJson returns ok:false without setting the read cooldown. Every get() call reads the file again, parses it, logs 'settings damaged', and runs setAsideDamaged's retrying(), which blocks the main thread in Atomics.wait for 25+50+75+100 = 250 ms. get() is called on every curlfetch request, every plugin file served (plugins.list), skin.css, settings:get and more, so the main process freezes repeatedly. `loaded` also never becomes true, so every set() of the session goes to `pending` and nothing is ever written. keys.js readAll (66) and autosave.js readState (78) have the same uncooled rename-retry path.
findings.scenario: settings.json is truncated (a crash before 0.1.55's fsync, a sync conflict copy), and the folder or a program holding the file refuses the rename. Each request, plugin module load or settings read then blocks main for about 250 ms and logs one more 'settings damaged' line. All settings the user changes this session are silently dropped, and no damagedNotice is shown, because the notice is set only when the rename succeeds.
findings.evidence: settings.js:119-127: the parse-failure branch calls setAsideDamaged(p) on every call and returns {ok:false} without touching readFailUntil (the cooldown is set only in the read-error branch at 108-112). settings.js:85-94 setAsideDamaged -> retrying() (76-83) with Atomics.wait 25*(i+1) ms for 4 retries. settings.js:162-199: !loaded keeps every set() in pending. curlfetch.install's enabled() calls settings.get() per request (main.js:44-47). plugins.js:72-84 list() calls settings.get() and is called for each /plugins/ file in serveFile (main.js:191).
findings.fix: Remember a failed set-aside (set readFailUntil, or a 'damaged' flag with its mtime) and skip the parse and rename until the file changes. Raise damagedNotice in that case too, saying the settings cannot be saved. Do the same in keys.js and autosave.js.
findings.why: I read settings.js at ce4415ec and the path is real. readJson (97-128) sets readFailUntil only in the read-error branch (109-112). The parse-failure branch (119-127) calls setAsideDamaged(p) on every call. When the rename keeps failing with EPERM, EBUSY or EACCES, retrying() (77-84) runs four Atomics.wait sleeps of 25, 50, 75 and 100 ms, so about 250 ms on the main thread. readJson then returns {ok:false} with damagedNotice left unset. get() (162-189) leaves `loaded` false on ok:false, so every later get() reads, parses, logs and retries the rename again. set() (191-199) keeps every patch in `pending` and never writes it, and the user is never told. get() is called on hot paths: curlfetch's enabled() runs per request (main.js:45, curlfetch.js:303), plus settings:get (main.js:1155), skin (254) and plugins.js list() (76, 89, 116, 121). So the repeated stall is reachable. keys.js readAll (59-71) and autosave.js readState (71-82) have the same uncooled set-aside retry. keys.js refuses the write (forWrite throws), so the repeated stall is the only problem there. This is not a known entry. verified.json:87-91 in review_full_2026-11-07 is the earlier finding that "any parse error counts as an empty store", and setAsideDamaged is its fix; this finding is about how that fix behaves when the rename itself fails. I found nothing in BUGS.md. The trigger is rare: the file must be readable but impossible to rename, for example a sync client, an antivirus scan or a folder ACL holding it without share-delete. In that state a write of settings.json would most likely fail anyway, so losing the settings matters less than the repeated 250 ms stalls and the missing notice. That makes it nice, not should. The suggested fix is sound: remember the failed set-aside, keyed by the file's mtime and size, skip the parse and the rename until the file changes, and set a notice that settings cannot be saved.

findings.claim: A request body goes to os.tmpdir() as scumble-curl-<pid>-<random>.bin and is deleted only in finish()/cleanup when the curl process closes. A quit, crash or kill during an upload leaves the file behind. Nothing removes old ones at start. The file holds the user's picture (an upload of a crop or a whole picture to a provider), and mode 0600 means nothing on Windows.
findings.scenario: The user starts a Comfy Cloud or fal run that uploads a large PNG (a 15k whole-picture upscale is hundreds of MB) and quits Scumble, or the app crashes, while curl is still sending. The process exits before child 'close' fires, so drop() never runs. Each such quit leaves a multi-hundred-MB copy of the user's image in %TEMP%, and it accumulates over sessions.
findings.evidence: curlfetch.js:117 drop() is called only from cleanup() (155) inside finish() (157-159), from the spawn failure (139), from the write failure (124) and from the early abort (129). No startup sweep exists for the `scumble-curl-*` prefix (grep finds none), and install() (315-323) does none.
findings.fix: At install(), unlink `scumble-curl-*.bin` files in os.tmpdir() whose pid is not the running process, or keep a Set of live body files and unlink them synchronously on process 'exit' / app 'will-quit'. Simpler still: pass small bodies on stdin and only large ones by file.
findings.why: I read curlfetch.js in the worktree. hop() writes every request body to os.tmpdir()/scumble-curl-<pid>-<hex>.bin (line 120-122). The only thing that removes it is drop() (117), and drop() runs only from the write failure (124), the abort before spawn (129), the spawn failure (139), the bad-HTTP-head branch (206, via cleanup) and finish() (159). finish() runs only after the child's stdout 'end' and 'close' events, and even then the unlink is async (fs.promises.unlink). If the main process exits, crashes or is killed while curl is still uploading, none of those paths finishes, so the file stays. main.js's start-up (1486-1494) sweeps only documents' unfinished saves (documents.sweep()); its will-quit handler aborts documents and fileSaves only. Nothing sweeps the scumble-curl-* prefix: grep finds the prefix only in curlfetch.js and in the test (tools/curlfetch_test.js:240, which checks for leftovers only within one test process). install() (315-323) does no cleanup. So a crash or quit during a large provider upload (a whole-picture upscale at 15k) leaves a copy of the user's picture in %TEMP%, possibly hundreds of MB, and these build up over time. Nothing in docs/BUGS.md or the two verified.json files covers it. I rated it nice, not should: it happens only when the app dies in the middle of an upload, and %TEMP% is per-user, so the privacy point is weak. The fix direction is right and has a precedent in the code: a start-up sweep of scumble-curl-*.bin whose pid is not the current process, like documents.sweep().

findings.claim: WaveSpeed's edit does not set ctx.jobDone when a Cancel lands during the final picture download. index.js then says the provider 'may still finish the job and charge it', when the job has in fact completed and is charged. fal (downloadResult) and Replicate (`completed`) both set jobDone for the same case.
findings.scenario: A WaveSpeed edit completes. The user presses Cancel while downloadImage fetches the CDN URL. The status line reads 'Scumble stopped waiting for WaveSpeedAI, which may still finish the job and charge it' instead of 'the job had already finished ... and is charged; its picture was not kept'.
findings.evidence: wavespeed.js edit 304-319: submitAndWait, then downloadImage at 314, with no try/catch that sets ctx.jobDone. index.js 320-329 picks its words by ctx.jobDone. fal.js downloadResult 303-310 and replicate.js 247-249 do set it. wavespeed.js layers() sets caller.jobDone at 348, but edit() does not.
findings.fix: Set ctx.jobDone = true right after submitAndWait returns in edit(), as layers() does.
findings.why: I read wavespeed.js edit() at 301-319. submitAndWait (368-392) returns only when the status is "completed" and throws otherwise. edit() then calls util.downloadImage at 314 with no try/catch. downloadImage (util.js 190-209) checks ctx.signal before each try and rethrows an abort, so a Cancel during the CDN fetch reaches index.js 318-329 while ctx.jobDone is still unset (grep finds only line 348 in layers()). The user then reads the fallback text, "Scumble stopped waiting for WaveSpeedAI, which may still finish the job and charge it", although the job had finished and is charged. fal sets ctx.jobDone in the same case (downloadResult 303-310, and `completed` at 289), Replicate too (`completed`, 247-249), and so do WaveSpeed's own layers() (348), ark.js 551 and oxen.js 642. The ctx in edit() is the object index.js holds: generate() hands it on unchanged and fitPictures does not replace it. This is not in BUGS.md. It is not in either verified.json: their WaveSpeed entries are about poll retries, the cancel URL / util.sleep and readError, not the jobDone wording. The fix direction is right: put `ctx.jobDone = true` right after submitAndWait returns, as layers() does. The non-abort error that follows ("no output") is not changed by the flag. Only the wording is wrong; no pixels or money are lost, so nice.

findings.claim: The MAIN-2 keep-for-a-gone-page path now fires for a Split into layers run, because every split adapter returns the base's bytes as out.bytes. It saves only the base plate as a 'brought back' picture and logs 'the picture is kept'. The paid layers are still dropped after 10 minutes in layerParts. docs/BUGS.md's entry still says a split has no bytes and is dropped whole.
findings.scenario: The window crashes or reloads during a ModelArk, WaveSpeed or Oxen split of 16 layers. The answer comes. pageGone() is true, so the base (out[0]) is written to results/ and noted. The new page opens it as a separate document. The 16 charged layers stay unasked in layerParts until LAYER_PARTS_KEEP_MS expires. The log says the picture is kept, so it looks as if the run was recovered.
findings.evidence: index.js 342-386 (the `out && out.bytes && hooks.pageGone()` branch makes no exception for `split`), then 394 keepLayerParts. ark.js 575, wavespeed.js 361 and oxen.js layers all return `bytes: out[0].bytes`. docs/BUGS.md line 52-54 describes the old behaviour.
findings.fix: Skip the local keep for kind 'layers' (or keep every layer with its boxes under one note), and update the BUGS.md entry.
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. In providers/index.js `edit`, the MAIN-2 branch at line 342 runs on `out && out.bytes && hooks.pageGone()` and has no exception for `split`. main.js:1260 passes `pageGone` for every provider:edit, splits included. All three split adapters return the base plate as `out.bytes`: ark.js:575, wavespeed.js:361 and oxen.js:652 all return `bytes: out[0].bytes`, and ark.js:523 says the base comes first. So when the window goes away during a split, only the base PNG is written to results/ and noted. The warn line says "the picture is kept (...), so the window opens it". Then line 394 still runs `keepLayerParts(out.layers)`, whose token never reaches the new page, and the timer drops the charged layers after LAYER_PARTS_KEEP_MS (10 min). This overlaps the open docs/BUGS.md entry at line 52 ("A Split into layers run is lost if its window reloads or crashes"), which covers the loss of the paid layers. But that entry gives the cause as "a split answers with several layers and no `bytes`", which is no longer true. What this finding adds is the stale BUGS.md text, the base-only partial keep and the misleading "kept" log line. So I answer confirmed, not known, at nice severity: the money loss is the known, accepted limit, and the new part is a small, misleading partial recovery. Fix direction is right: skip the local keep when `split` is true, or keep every layer with its boxes under one note, and update the BUGS.md entry.

findings.claim: Comfy Cloud's Krea3ImageNode edit sends a preset aspect_ratio chosen by editAspect (up to 3 % off the emitted crop, 8 % when planned), but its answer never carries info.fit 'stretch'. runV2 replaces the answer's info with { node, model, job_id }. Every other Krea 3 route reports stretch for the same choice (Replicate, OpenRouter, Oxen, Comfy Router). Here the stitch center-crops a preset-shaped answer instead.
findings.scenario: Krea 3 Edit on Comfy Cloud runs on a selection the stitch could not widen to a preset (the crop spans a whole 1.30:1 picture). editAspect picks 4:3 (2.5 % off). The answer comes back 4:3. stitch.finishPixels sees sameAspect false (more than 1 % off) and center-crops about 1.25 % from each side before scaling. The result shifts against the base near the crop edges.
findings.evidence: comfycloud.js SHAPES.Krea3ImageNode 144-152 sets model.aspect_ratio from editAspect(v, { ratios: KREA3_ASPECTS }). runV2 1078 does `got.info = info` and legacy run 879 also sets no fit. host_provider.js 393 copies res.info.fit. stitch.js 631 decides between stretch and center crop. comfyrouter.js krea read and replicate.js inputFor (info.fit = a.fit) do report it.
findings.fix: In buildGraph or runV2, add fit: 'stretch' to the answer's info when the Krea3ImageNode edit sent a preset other than 'auto' (as comfyrouter's krea read does).
findings.why: I read the code and the claim holds. In comfycloud.js, SHAPES.Krea3ImageNode (lines 144-152) sends `editAspect(v, {ratios: KREA3_ASPECTS}).aspect` on an edit. It keeps only `.aspect` and drops the `fit: "stretch"` that util.editAspect (lines 348-356) returns alongside a preset (within FIT_SLACK 0.03, or the planned preset within PLANNED_SLACK 0.08). runV2 then sets `got.info = info` at line 1078, where info is `{ node, model, job_id }` plus optional nodeList and events. The legacy run at line 879 returns `{ node, model, prompt_id }` the same way. Nothing in providers/index.js adds a fit either (grep finds none). In host_provider.js line 393, info.fit is set only from `res.info.fit === "stretch"`. In stitch.js line 631, `sameAspect` falls back to comparing the answer against `emitted` within 1 %, and a miss means a center crop (line 632). The Comfy Cloud variant of recipes/krea_3.json does declare `limits.aspects` (lines 266-282), so prepareCrop (stitch.js 438-448) widens the crop to a preset when the picture allows it. In that common case the emitted shape matches the preset, so the 1 % emitted check passes anyway. The defect only shows when the crop cannot be widened, for example the whole picture at 1.30:1. editAspect then sends 4:3 (about 2.5 % off), the answer comes back 4:3, and the stitch center-crops about 1.25 % per side instead of stretching. The other routes report stretch for the same choice: replicate.js line 129 (`if (a.fit) info.fit = a.fit`) and comfyrouter.js line 678 (`info: { fit: "stretch" }` for Krea). The fix direction is right: in runV2 and the legacy run, add `fit: "stretch"` to the answer's info when the Krea3ImageNode edit sent a preset rather than "auto". I rate it nice: only an unwidenable crop within 3 % of a preset is hit, and the result is a small shift or scale at the crop's edges, not lost data.

findings.claim: Only the unsaved-changes path checks again after an await that the tab is still open. After the 'still working, close anyway?' question, closeDocument goes on even when the same tab was closed in the meantime. A second close then puts the tab on the closed list again and destroys the editor twice.
findings.scenario: A tab is busy, for example a provider run. The user presses Ctrl+W. The question opens, and its key handler stops propagation without preventDefault, so the menu accelerator fires. The user presses Ctrl+W again, and a second closeDocument(host.editor) asks the same question a second time. The user answers Close on both. The first call removes, remembers and destroys the tab. The second call continues past the confirm: removeEditor emits 'removed' again, saveAll runs, and rememberClosed(editor) pushes a second entry for the same tab (Reopen Closed Tab then brings it back twice). editor.destroy() also runs a second time. The same happens when close_document from an agent, with remember false, closes the tab while the user's question is open: the user's Close then puts the tab on the closed list after all.
findings.evidence: shell.js 279 is the only check that the editor is still in host.editors(), and it is made on entry. Line 295 awaits dialogs.confirm. The dirty path re-checks at 298 (`!host.editors().includes(editor)`), but the busy path does not. Lines 304-312 then call host.removeEditor, host.saveAll, host.rememberClosed and editor.destroy unconditionally. rememberClosed (host_documents.js 321-331) pushes a new entry whenever ed.base is set.
findings.fix: After the confirm, add `if (!host.editors().includes(editor)) return false;`, as the dirty path has. Or keep a per-editor `_closing` flag that a second call returns on.
findings.why: I read renderer/shell.js closeDocument (281-313). The check that the tab is still open (`host.editors().includes(editor)`) runs at entry (282) and again only on the dirty path after askDocument and after the save (298, 301). After the busy question `await dialogs.confirm(... still working ...)` (295) there is no such check, so a call that waited on that question goes on to forgetDocument, host.removeEditor, saveAll, host.rememberClosed and editor.destroy (305-312) even when the tab closed while the question was open. The reentry is reachable. The Ctrl+W accelerator (main.js 749) sends `close-tab` and shell.js 1279 calls `closeDocument(host.editor)`, with no `dialogs.openCount()` gate. dialogs.js onKey only calls stopImmediatePropagation for Ctrl+W (no preventDefault), and an Electron menu accelerator fires anyway. So a second Ctrl+W on the still-open busy tab stacks a second question. The agent route is real too: commands_docs.js 83 closes with `force: true, remember: a.remember !== false`, which skips the question, so a user's pending Close afterwards still runs rememberClosed and ignores the agent's remember:false. The damage is small. host_state.js removeEditor is guarded by `i >= 0`, so the second removal does nothing. destroy() null-checks the compositor, so a second destroy is mostly harmless. destroy() does not clear `base`, though, so rememberClosed (host_documents.js 321-331) captures getValue again and pushes a second closed entry for the same tab. reopenClosed (343ff) pops entries with no check by id, so Reopen Closed Tab brings the same document back twice. No pixels are lost, so severity is nice. The fix direction is right: after the confirm, add `if (!host.editors().includes(editor)) return false;`, as the dirty path does. The entry is not in docs/BUGS.md or in either verified.json. The nearby verified.json entries are about rememberClosed's flush race and ask()'s window listener, which are different defects.

findings.claim: When New in a tab of its own does not produce a canvas, the new tab is closed. This covers a refused size and a failed upload into the local store, and the Cancel the code means it for. The tab's status line, which held the reason, is gone with it, and the original tab says nothing.
findings.scenario: The user clicks New in a tab with work. In the fresh tab they enter a size, and editor.newCanvas fails: the upload to the local store throws, or the size is refused with 'Width and height must be at least 16 pixels.'. That reason goes only to fresh's status line. Because `!fresh.base`, newCanvasInTab closes fresh and activates the original tab, so the click seems to do nothing. A real Cancel is handled the same way, which is intended, but a failure cannot be told from it.
findings.evidence: shell.js 189-198: `await fresh.newCanvas(); if (!fresh.base && host.editors().includes(fresh)) { await closeDocument(fresh, { force: true, remember: false }); if (host.editors().includes(editor)) activate(editor); }`. inpaint_ed_histpanel.js 355-405: every early return and the catch of newCanvas only call this.setStatus on the fresh editor.
findings.fix: Before closing fresh, copy its status to the original tab when it is not the cancel line, for example `if (fresh.status && !/cancelled/i.test(fresh.status)) editor.setStatus(fresh.status, fresh.statusKind)`. Or have newCanvas return whether the user cancelled.
findings.why:
I read renderer/shell.js 189-198. `newCanvasInTab` creates `fresh` with no base (`newDocument` makes an empty InpaintEditor), awaits `fresh.newCanvas()`, and closes `fresh` whenever `!fresh.base`. Then it activates the original tab, which gets no line of its own.

In renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js 355-435, every way `newCanvas` can fail before `setBasePixels` returns quietly after a `setStatus` on that same editor. That covers the size the parser cannot read, the cancel, the under-16 refusal, and the catch around `makeCanvas` / `uploadCanvas` ("Could not create the canvas: ..."). So it leaves `base` null. The reason lands only in `fresh.status` and `fresh.statusEl` (inpaint_canvas.js 674 `setStatus` writes only this editor's nodes), and the tab is then closed with `remember: false`. The catch's `console.error` is the only trace left.

`editor.newCanvasTab`'s own `.catch` (shell.js 171) does not help: `newCanvas` catches its own errors and never rejects. The case is real but rare (a failed upload into the local store, or `makeCanvas` throwing). The size refusal is mostly blocked by the dialog's min 16, and the cancel case is intended. Nothing is lost, because the original document stays untouched, so this is nice.

The fix direction is right: copy `fresh.status` and `fresh.statusKind` to `editor` before the close when they are not the cancel line, or have `newCanvas` return a cancelled/failed result. Not found in docs/BUGS.md or in either verified.json; this feature is new in 0.1.55.

findings.claim: The assistant keeps every event of a chat for its whole life, with no cap (Help caps at 500). That includes one text_delta per streamed chunk and every screenshot as a full data URL in tool_end. At every turn end, store.save writes all those pictures again as files, even though the history prunes to 3.
findings.scenario: A long chat with 80 screenshot calls holds about 12-16 MB of base64 in main's events. Each turn end rewrites all 80+ JPEGs plus a JSON file with thousands of text_delta records. Files beyond the current count, left by earlier saves, stay in the folder after the history's prune lowers the total. openChat loads it all back into memory.
findings.evidence: index.js:306-311 emit pushes to this.events with no cap. 700 emits text_delta per chunk. 852-859 tool_end carries `image: data:...;base64,...`. saveChat 561 passes { events: this.events }. store.js:54-61 strips events and history into images and writes every one with writeFile on each save. help.js:89 caps its own events at 500.
findings.fix: Do not store text_delta events (the assistant:text event holds the whole text). Keep tool_end images only for the last few cards, or as a marker to a file written once. Cap the event list.
findings.why:
The claim holds in the code. In electron/main/assistant/index.js:306-311, emit() pushes every event onto this.events and never caps the list. help.js:88-89 caps its own list at 500, but the assistant has no such cap. The list is cleared only by reset, resetAll, deleteChat and openChat (434, 576, 554, 531), never within a chat.

Line 700 emits one text_delta per streamed chunk, and line 714 also emits the whole text as assistant:text. renderer/assistant.js:860 replay() skips text_delta ("the text comes whole"), so storing those events helps nothing.

tool_end (852-859) carries the screenshot as a full data URL. state() at 460 sets image to null before the panel gets it, and openChat goes through state() as well. So after a reload or reopen, no stored event image is ever shown.

saveChat (559-563) runs at the end of every turn and passes { events: this.events }. store.js save() (39-66) runs strip() over both the events and the history and writes every picture again with writeFile each time. The history is pruned to keepImages=3 at index.js:682, but the events keep every screenshot. So each turn end rewrites all of the chat's pictures (the disk work grows with the square of the chat's length), and openChat/load reads them all back into main's memory.

Stale files also stay behind. Pictures are numbered 1..N in strip order, so when the history prune lowers N, the files above N remain in the folder until the chat is deleted or pruned. The leftover is bounded per prune, so the disk leak is small.

Nothing here loses or corrupts data. It is a growing memory and disk cost in long chats (about 100-200 kB per screenshot), so nice is the right severity. The suggested fix fits: don't keep text_delta events, drop or mark tool_end images after the live card, and cap the list. Not in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json. The external review's text_delta entry is about the renderer's scroll layout, which is a different defect.

findings.claim: The lines "The user undid your last turn." and "(your previous answer was stopped ...)" come after the layer list. The 1,500-character cut keeps only the first 1,400 characters, so on a document with many layers both lines are dropped.
findings.scenario: A document with about 35 or more layers, or long layer names. The user clicks Undo this turn and then asks "try again". chat.undone is consumed (index.js:680), but the note the model gets ends at "... (N layers; call list_layers for the rest)". The model is never told its work was undone and builds on layers it believes it made.
findings.evidence: prompt.js:68-77 pushes docs, then layers, then undone and stopped. 79-82 slices to 1400 and appends the layer-count line. index.js:679-680 consumes chat.undone once.
findings.fix: Put the undone and stopped lines (and the pinned-document line) before the layer list, or append them after the cut.
findings.why: Read prompt.js stateNote (64-84). The lines go in this order: the document lines, then every layer line (74), then "The user undid your last turn." (76) and the stopped line (77). When the joined note is longer than 1,500 characters, it is cut to its first 1,400 characters at the last newline, and only the "... (N layers; call list_layers for the rest)" line is added (79-81). So on a long note both trailing lines are always lost. The caller, index.js 669-680, passes the whole list_layers answer with no limit, then sets chat.undone = false right after building the note, so the flag is spent even when its line was cut. turnUndone (538-548) tells the model nothing else: emit("note") only adds a UI event to this.events and record() only writes to the log, and neither touches chat.history. chat.stopped is reset the same way at 688. A layer line is about 25-45 characters, so roughly 35-50 layers (fewer with long names or several open documents) is enough to trigger it, and documents with many result layers reach that. Nothing in BUGS.md or either verified.json mentions stateNote or the undone line. The fix the reviewer suggests (put the undone and stopped lines before the layer list, or add them after the cut) is the right one. The outcome is a confused agent turn, not lost pixels, so nice.

findings.claim: Stop while an ask card waits resolves the ask with false. runCall then records the user's decline: "the user declined; do not reach the same effect another way". The chat is also not marked stopped, because only a stream abort sets chat.stopped.
findings.scenario: The model asks to generate and the user presses Stop to rephrase. The history now says the user declined generating, and the system rules (prompt.js:17-18) tell the model not to reach that effect another way. On the next turn ("use a lower denoise and render") the model is told the user refused rendering, and gets no "(stopped)" note.
findings.evidence: index.js:321 `if (this.pending) { this.pending.resolve(false); ...}`. 806-810: `if (!allowed) { this.lastWasDecline = true; return errorResult("the user declined; ...") }`. 734 pushes those results. 692 ends with done("stopped") without chat.stopped = true.
findings.fix: In runCall, check turn.stopped after ask() resolves and return "stopped by the user" instead of the decline text. Set chat.stopped = true on every stopped exit.
findings.why:
The path is real. stop() (index.js:316-323) sets turn.stopped, aborts the signal and calls this.pending.resolve(false). ask() (965) is a plain promise that only that resolve settles, so in runCall (806-810) `allowed` is false: lastWasDecline is set and the result is "the user declined; do not reach the same effect another way". The step loop (731-735) pushes that result into chat.history. The next iteration then returns at 692, `if (turn.stopped) return this.done(chat, turn, "stopped")`, and that line does not set chat.stopped. Only the stream paths (706, 709) set it, and done() (1010) does not either. So the next turn's stateNote (679) has no "(your previous answer was stopped before it finished)" line, although appendUserText's comment (1182) says that line is meant for exactly this case. The same missing note hits a Stop during a running tool call: 843 returns "stopped by the user", then 692 ends the turn without the flag.

Two things soften it. "Stop counts as a decline" is the intended design: ask()'s own comment says so, and PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:630 and :2578 say "Stop = deny" and "Stop declines every pending ask". So the decline wording follows the plan; the defect is only that the model is never told the decline was a Stop. And a fresh user request ("render with lower denoise") is a new instruction the model will usually follow, so the harm is a misleading history line, not lost pixels or money.

The fix direction is right and small: in runCall, after ask() resolves, return "stopped by the user" when turn.stopped is set; and set chat.stopped = true on the 692 exit too. The finding is not in docs/BUGS.md or either verified.json (I grepped for declined and lastWasDecline).

findings.claim: lastTurnCost is added to on every usage event and reset only by New chat, Open chat and Reset, never at turn:start. So "last turn $x" shows the running total of the panel's session.
findings.scenario: Three turns of $0.02 each: after the third the panel shows "last turn $0.0600".
findings.evidence: assistant.js:561-563 `lastTurnCost += e.cost.amount`. turn:start 528-533 does not reset it. Resets only at 727, 753, 812.
findings.fix: Set lastTurnCost = 0 in the turn:start case.
findings.why: renderer/assistant.js:562 adds e.cost.amount to lastTurnCost on every "usage" event. Main sends one such event per model step: electron/main/assistant/index.js:713 emits `{usage: res.usage, cost: this.costOf(chat, res.usage)}`, which is the cost of that step alone, not a running total. The turn:start case (528-533) resets cards, busy and the button but leaves lastTurnCost alone. The only resets are at 727, 753 and 812 (open chat, new chat and reset paths), where usage is set to null too. turn:start does reach the panel: index.js:402 emits it through emit() (306-310) as `{type: "turn:start", ...}`. So during one panel session "last turn $x" (showCost, 613) keeps adding up across turns. After turn three of a fresh chat it shows the same sum as "this chat", against docs/ASSISTANT.md:210, which says the footer shows the last turn. It is display only, so no money is spent and no document is touched: nice. The fix is right: set lastTurnCost = 0 in the turn:start case, so it still adds up the several step events within one turn. Neither BUGS.md nor either verified.json mentions lastTurnCost.

findings.claim: restoreTurn (named snapshots from the Undo history panel and MCP restore_snapshot; also the assistant's Undo this turn) applies a whole-document `turn` snapshot, size and geometry included, at once. It skips every guard that historyStepNow applies to the same step kind: it does not check turnBlocked() for a running provider, local, Each area or load job, it does not wait for edits held by trackEdit (crop, extend, resize, merge into base, flatten, which push their step and write after an upload), and it does not check gestureHeld.
findings.scenario: The user takes a snapshot of a 6000 x 4000 document, crops it to 3000 x 2000, and starts an API Generate on a selection. While the run is paid for and running, they click the snapshot's Restore button: the document is 6000 x 4000 again, and the result lands at the crop coordinates of the 3000 x 2000 geometry, in the wrong place. A second case: Restore clicked while a Merge into base or a crop is still uploading. That edit's tail then writes its new base or layer list over the restored snapshot. In both cases the undo/redo of a canvas or turn step would have been refused with 'a job still running on this document would land where the picture was'.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_history.js restoreTurn 244-252: cancelPreviews, turnSnapshot, pushUndoSnapshot, applySnapshot(snap) with no turnBlocked, no _pendingEdits wait and no queueHistory. restoreSnapshot 294-299 calls it directly. Compare historyStepNow 993-1021: `while (this._pendingEdits && this._pendingEdits.size) await ...`, held(), and `if ((snap.kind === "canvas" || snap.kind === "turn") && this.turnBlocked())` with the release-review note. applySnapshot `turn` 619-623 restores geometry, width and height. inpaint_ed_geometry.js turnBlocked 624-633. mergeDownNow (inpaint_ed_layers.js 361-368) sets this.base and filters this.layers after its await.
findings.fix: Run restoreSnapshot through the history queue: queueHistory(async () => { wait for _pendingEdits; refuse when gestureHeld() or turnBlocked() returns a reason, with the same status line; then restoreTurn }). Let the MCP command and the panel button report the refusal. Give the assistant's restoreTurn the same checks.
findings.why: This repeats canvas-b/snapshot-restore-skips-turnblocked in docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json (should, small effort, confirmed there). That entry makes the same claim about restoreSnapshot and restoreTurn, names the same three callers (the Restore button in the Undo history panel, MCP restore_snapshot, the assistant's Undo this turn) and proposes the same fix. Its line numbers point into the old single inpaint_canvas.js. The defect is still in the split code at ce4415ec. In renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js, restoreTurn (lines 244-252) calls cancelPreviews, turnSnapshot, pushUndoSnapshot and applySnapshot. It never checks turnBlocked() or gestureHeld(), never waits for _pendingEdits, and does not go through queueHistory. restoreSnapshot (294-299) calls restoreTurn directly. The callers add no guard either: commands_edit.js restore_snapshot (197-204) checks only that the snapshot exists, inpaint_modal.js:562 calls ed.restoreSnapshot straight from the button, and assistant_turns.js:83 calls ed.restoreTurn. historyStepNow (987-1023), by contrast, waits for _pendingEdits, checks held() and refuses canvas/turn steps while turnBlocked() returns a reason. So the finding is correct, but it adds nothing new beyond the 2026-11-07 entry.

findings.claim: With the auth type "header", the user names the header (authHeaders 26). Every proxied request, probe and objectInfo fetch carries it with redirect "follow". Neither path drops a user-named header on a cross-origin redirect: undici drops only authorization, cookie and proxy-authorization, and curlfetch drops only its fixed KEY_HEADERS list. The secret therefore goes to whatever host the remote ComfyUI or its reverse proxy redirects to. The ComfyUI window restricts the same headers to the target's origin (comfyview.js applyHeaders), so the two paths treat the same secret differently.
findings.scenario: A remote ComfyUI behind a reverse proxy that checks `X-Pod-Token` and answers /view with a 302 to presigned object storage (an S3/R2 bucket) or a login page on another host. Every `` the editor loads through scumble://app/comfy/view sends X-Pod-Token to the storage host's access logs.
findings.evidence: comfy.js:20-29 authHeaders type "header" -> { [a.header]: s }. comfy.js:100-109 builds init = { method, headers: {...this.headers...}, redirect: "follow" } and calls the global fetch. curlfetch.js:39 KEY_HEADERS is a fixed set and 269 filters only those on an origin change. comfy.js:134 probe and comfyview.js:710 objectInfo send the same headers with the default redirect follow. Compare comfyview.js:577-586, which sends headers only when sameOrigin.
findings.fix: In ComfyClient.fetch/proxy/probe, use redirect: "manual" and follow by hand, dropping this.headers' keys when the next hop's origin differs from this.url's. Or keep "follow" and have curlfetch take a per-request list of headers to drop on an origin change.
findings.why: This finding is already recorded as part 2 of finding S2 in docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json (verdict "partly", severity low). The evidence field there makes the same point: comfy.js:105 (proxy), :134 (probe) and ComfyClient.fetch follow redirects carrying this.headers, undici drops only authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie and host, so an auth.type "header" value goes on to the redirect target, and the ComfyUI window limits the same headers to the target's origin. Its fix also matches: redirect "manual", follow the hops by hand, and re-send the headers only while the origin is the same. S2 was not part of the H1 hardening (S1, S5, S6, S9a, S8).
